title.zh: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登
title.en: Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng
title.raw: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登 Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng

sentences.zh: 苻丕 苻登

translations.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi and Fu Deng (biographies)

sentences.zh: 苻丕，字永叔，堅之長庶子也。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, styled Yongshu, was Fu Jian's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, whose courtesy name was Yongshu, was the eldest of Emperor Xuanzhao of Qin's sons born to a concubine.

sentences.zh: 少而聰彗好學，博綜經史。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and comet-bright, fond of learning, broadly comprehensive in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was quick-witted and bookish, with wide learning in the classical canon and historical records.

sentences.zh: 堅與言將略，嘉之，命鄧羌教以兵法。

translations.literal: Fu Jian spoke with him about generalship and strategy, praised him, and ordered Deng Qiang to teach him military methods.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian discussed strategy with him, was impressed, and assigned Deng Qiang to school him in the art of war.

sentences.zh: 文武才幹亞於苻融，為將善收士卒情，出鎮於鄴，東夏安之。

translations.literal: In civil and military talent he was second to Fu Rong; as a general he was good at winning officers' and soldiers' feelings; when he went out to garrison Ye, the eastern Xia was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His gifts in civil and military affairs ranked just below Fu Rong's; as a commander he knew how to win the loyalty of the ranks. Posted to Ye, he brought stability to the eastern heartland.

sentences.zh: 堅敗歸長安，丕為慕容垂所逼，自鄴奔枋頭。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated and returned to Chang'an, Pi was pressed by Murong Chui and fled from Ye to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat at Fei River, Fu Pi was driven by Murong Chui to abandon Ye and flee to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 堅之死也，丕復入鄴城，將收兵趙、魏，西赴長安。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian died, Pi again entered Ye city, intending to gather troops in Zhao and Wei and go west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Fu Jian's death reached him, Fu Pi reoccupied Ye, planning to raise forces in Zhao and Wei and march west toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 會幽州刺史王永、平州刺史苻沖頻為垂將平規等所敗，乃遣昌黎太守宋敞焚燒和龍、薊城宮室，率眾三萬進屯壺關，遣使招丕。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Youzhou Wang Yong and Inspector of Pingzhou Fu Chong had repeatedly been defeated by Chui's general Ping Gui and others; therefore they sent Administrator of Changli Song Chang to burn the palace buildings at Helong and Jicheng, led thirty thousand men forward to encamp at Huguan, and sent envoys to summon Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Yong of Youzhou and Fu Chong of Pingzhou had suffered repeated defeats at the hands of Murong Chui's officer Ping Gui. They dispatched Song Chang, Administrator of Changli, to torch the palaces at Helong and Ji, moved thirty thousand troops up to Huguan, and sent messengers urging Fu Pi to join them.

sentences.zh: 丕乃去鄴，率男女六萬餘口進如潞川。

translations.literal: Pi then left Ye and led more than sixty thousand men and women advancing to Lucuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi accordingly quit Ye and marched more than sixty thousand people toward the Lu River basin.

sentences.zh: 驃騎張蠔、并州刺史王騰迎之，入據晉陽，始知堅死問，舉哀于晉陽，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: Cavalry-in-Command Zhang Hao and Inspector of Bingzhou Wang Teng welcomed him; they entered and occupied Jinyang, where they first learned the news of Fu Jian's death; they observed mourning at Jinyang; the three armies wore white.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao, General of Agile Cavalry, and Wang Teng, Inspector of Bingzhou, received him; together they took Jinyang, where Fu Pi first received certain word of Fu Jian's death. The court mourned at Jinyang, and the entire host went into white mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 王永留苻沖守壺關，率騎一萬會丕，勸稱尊號，丕從之，乃乙太元十年僭即皇帝位於晉陽南。

translations.literal: Wang Yong left Fu Chong to defend Huguan, led ten thousand horsemen to join Pi, urged assuming the exalted title, Pi followed; thereupon in the tenth year of Taiyuan he usurped the imperial position south of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong left Fu Chong to hold Huguan, brought ten thousand cavalry to Fu Pi's camp, and urged him to take the throne; Fu Pi agreed. In the tenth year of the Eastern Jin Taiyuan era he presumptuously assumed the imperial title south of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 立堅行廟，太赦境內，改元曰太安。

translations.literal: He established Fu Jian's travelling shrine, greatly pardoned within the realm, and changed the era name to Taian.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a provisional ancestral shrine for Fu Jian, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout his domain, and adopted the reign title Taian.

sentences.zh: 置百官，以張蠔為侍中、司空，封上黨郡公；

translations.literal: He established the hundred officials; he appointed Zhang Hao as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, enfeoffing him as Duke of Shangdang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He installed a full bureaucracy, naming Zhang Hao Palace Attendant and Minister of Works with ducal rank in Shangdang;

sentences.zh: 王永為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、尚書令，進封清河公；

translations.literal: Wang Yong as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced enfeoffment as Duke of Qinghe;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong received the staff of authority and the posts of Palace Attendant, commander over all armies, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Director of the Masters of Writing, and was promoted to Duke of Qinghe;

sentences.zh: 王騰為散騎常侍、中軍大將軍、司隸校尉、陽平郡公；

translations.literal: Wang Teng as Regular Cavalier Attendant, General of the Central Army, Colonel Director of Retainers, and Duke of Yangping commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Teng became Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, General of the Central Army, Colonel Director of Retainers, and Duke of Yangping;

sentences.zh: 苻沖為左光祿大夫、尚書左僕射、西平王；

translations.literal: Fu Chong as Grand Master of the Left, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong was named Grand Master of the Left, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Xiping;

sentences.zh: 俱石子為衛將軍、濮陽公；

translations.literal: Ju Shizi as General Who Guards the Palace and Duke of Puyang;
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shizi was appointed General Who Guards the Palace and Duke of Puyang;

sentences.zh: 楊輔為尚書右僕射、濟陽公；

translations.literal: Yang Fu as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Jiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Jiyang;

sentences.zh: 王亮為護軍將軍、彭城公；

translations.literal: Wang Liang as General Who Protects the Army and Duke of Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang was named General Who Protects the Army and Duke of Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 強益耳、梁暢為侍中，徐義為吏部尚書，並封縣公。

translations.literal: Qiang Yier and Liang Chang as Palace Attendants, Xu Yi as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, all enfeoffed as county dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Yier and Liang Chang were made Palace Attendants, Xu Yi Minister of Personnel, each receiving county-level ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 自余封授各有差。

translations.literal: For the rest, enfeoffments and appointments each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: All other titles and fiefs were distributed according to merit and station.

sentences.zh: 是時安西呂光自西域還師，至於宜禾，堅涼州刺史梁熙謀閉境距之。

translations.literal: At this time Lü Guang the West Pacifier returned his army from the Western Regions, reaching Yihe; Liang Xi, Fu Jian's Inspector of Liangzhou, plotted to close the borders and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Lü Guang, General Who Pacifies the West, was marching home from the Tarim basin and reached Yihe. Liang Xi, whom Fu Jian had left as Inspector of Liangzhou, planned to shut the frontier and bar his passage.

sentences.zh: 高昌太守楊翰言於熙曰：「「呂光新定西國，兵強氣銳，其鋒不可當也。

translations.literal: Yang Han, Administrator of Gaochang, spoke to Xi, saying: "Lü Guang has newly pacified the western states; his troops are strong and his qi sharp; his edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Han, magistrate of Gaochang, warned Liang Xi: "Lü Guang has just subdued the Western Regions; his army is strong and his morale keen. You cannot meet that spearhead head-on.

sentences.zh: 度其事意，必有異圖。

translations.literal: Measuring the affair's intent, he is sure to have a different design.
translations.idiomatic: Judging his intentions, he must be planning something beyond a simple homecoming.

sentences.zh: 且今關中擾亂，京師存亡未知，自河已西迄於流沙，地方萬里，帶甲十萬，鼎峙之勢實在今日。

translations.literal: Moreover now Guanzhong is disturbed and chaotic; the capital's survival or destruction is unknown; from west of the River to the shifting sands, the territory is ten thousand li, with one hundred thousand armored men—the tripod-standoff situation is truly today.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guanzhong is in turmoil and the fate of the capital uncertain. From the Yellow River west to the desert stretches ten thousand li of territory and a hundred thousand armored men. The moment for a three-way standoff of powers is now.

sentences.zh: 若光出流沙，其勢難測。

translations.literal: If Guang exits the shifting sands, his momentum will be hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Guang emerges from the desert, his next move will be impossible to predict.

sentences.zh: 高梧穀口，水險之要，宜先守之而奪其水。

translations.literal: Gaowu Valley mouth is a choke point of water peril; you ought first to hold it and seize their water.
translations.idiomatic: The mouth of Gaowu Gorge is a choke point where water is the decisive terrain; seize it first and cut off their supply of water.

sentences.zh: 彼既窮渴，自然投戈。

translations.literal: When they are exhausted and thirsty, naturally they will cast aside weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Once they are parched and at their wits' end, they will lay down their arms of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 如其以遠不守，伊吾之關亦可距也。

translations.literal: If because of distance you do not hold it, the pass of Yiwu can also resist.
translations.idiomatic: If you decline to hold a distant line, you can still block him at the Yiwu frontier pass.

sentences.zh: 若度此二要，雖有子房之策，難為計矣。

translations.literal: If you cross these two crucial points, though you had Zhang Liang's stratagems, it would be hard to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Let him past those two barriers and even a strategist like Zhang Liang could not save you.

sentences.zh: 地有所必爭，真此機也。

translations.literal: There is ground that must be contested; truly this is the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Some ground history itself demands you fight for; this is that moment.

sentences.zh: 」熙弗從。

translations.literal: " Xi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi rejected the counsel.

sentences.zh: 美水令犍為張統說熙曰：「主上傾國南討，覆敗而還。

translations.literal: Zhang Tong of Qianwei, Magistrate of Meishui, persuaded Xi, saying: "The lord above tilted the whole state south to punish and was overturned in defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tong of Qianwei, magistrate of Meishui, urged Liang Xi: "Our sovereign staked the realm on the southern campaign and came home in ruinous defeat.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂擅兵河北，泓、沖寇逼京師，丁零雜虜，跋扈關、洛，州郡奸豪，所在風扇，王綱弛絕，人懷利己。

translations.literal: Murong Chui monopolizes troops north of the River; Hong and Chong raid and press the capital; Dingling miscellaneous barbarians run rampant in Guan and Luo; commandery and prefecture wicked magnates, everywhere wind fans; royal net slackens and breaks; people harbor benefiting self.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui dominates Hebei; Murong Hong and Murong Chong threaten the capital; Dingling and other tribes rampage through the Guanzhong and Luoyang regions; opportunists and strongmen stir insurrection wherever they can. Imperial authority has collapsed and every man looks to his own advantage.

sentences.zh: 今呂光回師，將軍何以抗也？

translations.literal: Now Lü Guang returns the army—how will the general resist?
translations.idiomatic: With Lü Guang's army marching home, how do you propose to stop him?

sentences.zh: 」熙曰：「誠深憂之，未知計之所出。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Truly I deeply worry; I do not know where a plan comes out.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi answered: "I share that fear, yet I see no clear course.

sentences.zh: 」統曰：「光雄果勇毅，明略絕人，今以蕩西域之威，擁歸師之銳，鋒若猛火之盛于原，弗可敵也。

translations.literal: " Tong said: "Guang is heroic, resolute, brave, and firm; his clear strategy surpasses others; now with the awe of having swept the Western Regions, embracing a returning army's sharpness, his edge is like fierce fire blazing on the plain—cannot be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tong replied: "Lü Guang is bold, decisive, and a born leader; his tactical sense is extraordinary. Fresh from conquering the west, his veterans will hit you like wildfire sweeping dry grass. They cannot be faced in open battle.

sentences.zh: 將軍世受殊恩，忠誠夙著，立勳王室，宜在於今。

translations.literal: The general generation after generation has received special favor; loyalty and sincerity have long been manifest; establishing merit for the royal house ought to be now.
translations.idiomatic: Your family has long enjoyed the dynasty's exceptional favor and a reputation for loyalty. If ever there was a time to serve the house of Fu, it is now.

sentences.zh: 行唐公洛，上之從弟，勇冠一時。

translations.literal: Duke of Xingtang Luo is the sovereign's younger male cousin; his bravery crowns the age.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Luo, Duke of Xingtang, is a cousin of the late emperor and the foremost warrior of his generation.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若奉為盟主，以攝眾望，推忠義以總率群豪，則光無異心也。

translations.literal: For the general's planning, nothing is like honoring him as covenant lord to gather multitudes' hope, promoting loyalty and righteousness to command the host of heroes—then Guang will have no different heart.
translations.idiomatic: The soundest plan is to acclaim Fu Luo as leader of the alliance, win the gentry's confidence, and rally the regional lords under the banner of loyalty. Lü Guang will then have no excuse to turn on you.

sentences.zh: 資其精銳，東兼毛興，連王統、楊璧，集四州之眾，掃凶逆于諸夏，甯帝室於關中，此桓文之舉也。

translations.literal: Relying on their picked troops, east annex Mao Xing, connect Wang Tong and Yang Bi, gather the four provinces' hosts, sweep fierce rebels in the various Xia, pacify the imperial house in Guanzhong—this is a Huan-Wen deed.
translations.idiomatic: Use his elite soldiers to absorb Mao Xing in the east, link arms with Wang Tong and Yang Bi, concentrate the armies of four provinces, purge the traitors from the heartland, and restore order in Guanzhong—that would be a deed worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen of Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 」熙又不從。

translations.literal: " Xi again did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Again Liang Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 殺洛於西海，以子胤為鷹揚將軍，率眾五萬距光於酒泉。

translations.literal: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed son Yin as General Who Displays Might, led fifty thousand hosts to resist Guang at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Fu Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Liang Yin General Who Displays Might, and sent fifty thousand men to block Lü Guang at Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守姚靜、晉昌太守李純以郡降光。

translations.literal: Yao Jing Administrator of Dunhuang and Li Chun Administrator of Jinchang surrendered their commanderies to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jing of Dunhuang and Li Chun of Jinchang yielded their prefectures to Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 胤及光戰于安彌，為光所敗。

translations.literal: Yin and Guang fought at Anmi; he was defeated by Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.

sentences.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙迎光，光殺之。

translations.literal: Peng Ji Administrator of Wuwei seized Xi and welcomed Guang; Guang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ji of Wuwei seized Liang Xi and handed him to Lü Guang, who put Liang Xi to death.

sentences.zh: 建威、西郡太守索泮，奮威、督洪池已南諸軍事、酒泉太守宋皓等，並為光所殺。

translations.literal: Suo Pan Administrator of Jianwei and Xijun, Song Hao Administrator of Fenwei who supervises military affairs south of Hongchi and of Jiuquan, and others, were all killed by Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan, who held the titles of General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xijun, and Song Hao, General Who Displays Might, commander south of Hongchi Pool, and Administrator of Jiuquan, among others, were all executed by Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Weichang, came fleeing from Guanzhong; he was appointed Grand Commandant and advanced enfeoffment as Prince of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's former Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Weichang, escaped from Guanzhong to join Fu Pi, who named him Grand Commandant and elevated him to Prince of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。

translations.literal: He appointed Wang Gun Administrator of Zhongshan as General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding as General Who Campaigns East, Shepherd of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao as General Who Garrisons the East, Supervisor of Jizhou Military Affairs, and Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo as General Who Campaigns West, Shepherd of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang as Grand General Who Garrisons the North, Supervisor of You and Bing Military Affairs—and all advanced rank to commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gun, Administrator of Zhongshan, became General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng. Fu Ding was named General Who Campaigns East, Governor of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng. Fu Shao received General Who Garrisons the East, command over all Jizhou forces, and the Marquisate of Chonghe. Fu Mo was appointed General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi. Fu Liang became Grand General Who Garrisons the North with authority over Youzhou and Bingzhou. Each was then promoted to ducal rank at the commandery level.

sentences.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang first held Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye city, they all surrendered to Chui; hearing Pi assumed the exalted title, they sent envoys apologizing for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had earlier occupied Changshan; during Murong Chui's siege of Ye they had all submitted to him. Learning that Fu Pi had declared himself emperor, they dispatched messengers to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。

translations.literal: Wang Gun firmly defended Boling and stood off against Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gun held out in Boling in a prolonged stalemate with Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。

translations.literal: Dou Chong General of the Left, Wang Tong Inspector of Qinzhou, Mao Xing Inspector of Hezhou, Wang Guang Inspector of Yizhou, Yang Bi Inspector of South Qinzhou, and Yang Ding General Who Guards the Palace, all held Longyou, sent envoys summoning Pi, requesting to punish Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong, Wang Tong of Qinzhou, Mao Xing of Hezhou, Wang Guang of Yizhou, Yang Bi of Southern Qinzhou, and Yang Ding, General Who Guards the Palace, all controlled the Longyou plateau. They sent envoys inviting Fu Pi to join them in a campaign against Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 丕大悅，以定為驃騎大將軍、雍州牧，沖為征西大將軍、梁州牧，統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍，璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。

translations.literal: Pi was greatly pleased; he appointed Ding as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Shepherd of Yongzhou, Chong as Grand General Who Campaigns West and Shepherd of Liangzhou, Tong as Grand General Who Garrisons the West, Xing as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bi as Grand General Who Campaigns South, all opening office with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes, adding Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, Guang as General Who Pacifies the West, all advancing position to Shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi was delighted. He named Yang Ding Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Yongzhou; Dou Chong Grand General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Liangzhou; Wang Tong Grand General Who Garrisons the West; Mao Xing Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; and Yang Bi Grand General Who Campaigns South—each with independent headquarters and honors matching the Three Excellencies—while adding the title Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant and appointing Wang Guang General Who Pacifies the West. All were promoted to provincial governor rank.

sentences.zh: 於是王永宣檄州郡曰：「大行皇帝棄背萬國，四海無主。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Yong proclaimed a call to arms to commanderies and prefectures, saying: "The great departed emperor abandoned and turned his back on the myriad states; within the four seas there is no lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong then issued a manifesto to the provinces: "The late emperor has left the realm, and the empire has no sovereign.

sentences.zh: 征東大將軍、長樂公，先帝元子，聖武自天，受命荊南，威振衡海，分陝東都，道被夷夏，仁澤光於宇宙，德聽侔于《下武》。

translations.literal: The Grand General Who Campaigns East, Duke of Changle, the late emperor's eldest son, sage-martial from Heaven, received mandate south of Jing, awe shakes Heng and sea, divided Shaan eastern capital, way covers Yi and Xia, benevolent grace shines on universe, virtuous hearing equals the 'Lower Wu'.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General Who Campaigns East, Duke of Changle, is the late emperor's firstborn: heaven-endowed in arms, entrusted with authority south of the Jing, his might rolls from the Heng range to the sea. He has shared the burden of the eastern capital, and his virtue embraces both barbarian and Chinese. His humane rule illuminates the cosmos, and his good name rivals the praise sung in the 'Lower Martial' ode of the Classic of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 永與司空蠔等謹順天人之望，以季秋吉辰奉公紹承大統，銜哀即事，棲穀總戎，枕戈待旦，志雪大恥。

translations.literal: Yong and Minister of Works Hao and others respectfully followed Heaven and men's hope; on an autumn auspicious day they honored the duke to continue the great line, bearing grief undertaking affairs, dwelling in hardship commanding troops, pillowing spear awaiting dawn, intent on washing the great shame.
translations.idiomatic: I, Wang Yong, together with Minister of Works Zhang Hao and others, have bowed to the will of Heaven and the people and, on an auspicious day in late autumn, installed our lord to carry on the imperial line. Though we mourn, we take up the work of state, endure hardship, and keep our weapons at hand, resolved to avenge this national disgrace.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂為封豕於關東，泓、沖繼凶於京邑，致乘輿播越，宗社淪傾。

translations.literal: Murong Chui became a great boar east of the Pass; Hong and Chong succeeded in viciousness at the capital region, causing the imperial carriage to be driven about, ancestral altars to sink and topple.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui rampages east of the mountains like a monstrous boar; Murong Hong and Murong Chong have brought ruin to the capital, forcing the throne into exile and casting down the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 羌賊姚萇，我之牧士，乘釁滔天，親行大逆，有生之巨賊也。

translations.literal: The Qiang bandit Yao Chang, our pasturing soldier, riding opportunity flooding Heaven, personally enacted great treason—among the living, a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang rebel Yao Chang, once a mere herdsman in our service, has exploited chaos to commit towering crimes and has personally murdered his sovereign—the greatest traitor alive.

sentences.zh: 永累葉受恩，世荷將相，不與驪山之戎、滎澤之狄共戴皇天，同履厚土。

translations.literal: Yong for accumulated generations received favor, generation after generation bore general and minister; I do not with the Rong of Lishan or the Di of Xingze together wear bright Heaven, together tread thick earth.
translations.idiomatic: My house has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations and has borne the responsibilities of general and minister. I refuse to stand under the same sky or walk the same earth as the Rong of Mount Li or the Di of the Xingze marshes—those who would betray their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 諸牧伯公侯或宛沛宗臣，或四七勳舊，豈忍舍破國之醜豎，縱殺君之逆賊乎！

translations.literal: You various shepherds, dukes, and marquises are either Wan-Pei imperial clansmen or four-seven meritorious elders—how could you bear to abandon the state's broken ugly brats, indulge the lord-killing rebellious villains!
translations.idiomatic: You governors and nobles are either kinsmen who stood with the house at Nanyang and Pei or veterans who earned your honors in the founding wars. Can you truly cast in your lot with upstarts who would shatter the realm or with regicides who stalk free?

sentences.zh: 主上飛龍九五，實協天心，靈祥休瑞，史不輟書，投戈效義之士三十餘萬，少康、光武之功可旬朔而成。

translations.literal: The lord above flies dragon nine-five, truly harmonizes Heaven's heart; numinous auspicious blessed omens, histories do not cease writing; men who cast spears and devote to righteousness exceed three hundred thousand; Shaokang and Guangwu's merit can be completed in ten days or a month.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign has ascended the throne as the true dragon; Heaven itself approves. Auspicious signs crowd the chronicles, and more than three hundred thousand men have already laid down private feuds to serve the righteous cause. The restoration achieved by Shaokang or Emperor Guangwu of Han can be repeated within weeks.

sentences.zh: 今以衛將軍俱石子為前軍師，司空張蠔為中軍都督。

translations.literal: Now we appoint General Who Guards the Palace Ju Shizi as Forward Army Strategist, Minister of Works Zhang Hao as Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shizi, General Who Guards the Palace, is named strategist of the vanguard; Minister of Works Zhang Hao commands the central army.

sentences.zh: 武將猛士，風烈雷震，志殄元凶，義無他顧。

translations.literal: Martial generals and fierce warriors, wind fierce thunder shake, intent on exterminating the chief culprit, in righteousness there is no other looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Our warriors move like wind and thunder, intent on destroying the arch-traitor, with no thought but duty.

sentences.zh: 永謹奉乘輿，恭行天罰。

translations.literal: Yong respectfully upholds the imperial carriage, reverently carries out Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I, Wang Yong, will escort the imperial regalia and execute Heaven's judgment upon the rebels.

sentences.zh: 君臣終始之義，在三忘軀之誠，戮力同之，以建晉、鄭之美。」

translations.literal: The righteousness of lord and minister from beginning to end, the sincerity of forgetting body in the three—exert strength together with it, to establish the beauty of Jin and Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Let every minister remember the bond that ties liege and vassal from first to last, and the duty that demands we risk our lives without hesitation. Join your strength to ours and help build a restoration as glorious as those of Jin and Zheng in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin attacked Wang Gun at Boling; by now grain was exhausted and arrows spent; the commandery merit officer Zhang Yi crossed the wall gathering a host responding to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin had long besieged Wang Gun in Boling; supplies were now exhausted. Zhang Yi, a clerical officer of the commandery, slipped over the walls and raised a party that opened the city to Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。

translations.literal: Gun ascended the city and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gun stood on the wall and rebuked him: "You were born a subject of Qin.

sentences.zh: 吾，卿之君也。

translations.literal: I am your lord.
translations.idiomatic: I am your lawful superior.

sentences.zh: 起眾應賊，號稱義兵，何名實相違之甚！

translations.literal: You raised a host responding to the bandit, calling it righteous troops—how name and reality contradict so greatly!
translations.idiomatic: You have rallied men for a rebel host yet call it a righteous militia—never was name further from truth!

sentences.zh: 卿兄往合鄉宗，親逐城主，天地不容，為世大戮。

translations.literal: Your elder brother formerly joined township lineage, personally drove out the city lord; Heaven and Earth do not tolerate, becoming the age's great execution.
translations.idiomatic: Your brother once rallied the local clans and personally drove out his rightful lord. Heaven and earth condemned him, and he died a traitor's death.

sentences.zh: 身滅未幾，卿復續之。

translations.literal: His body perished not long ago; you again continue it.
translations.idiomatic: His corpse is barely cold, and you take up his crime.

sentences.zh: 卿見為吾吏，親尋干戈，競為戎首，為爾君者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: You are seen as my official, personally seeking spears and halberds, competing to be war leader—for one who is your lord, is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: You serve under my command, yet you seize weapons and make yourself captain of mutiny. What lord could endure such subjects?

sentences.zh: 今人何取卿一切之功，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事！

translations.literal: Now people what take your every merit—how can they forget your unfilial unfilial affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine anyone will honor your petty coup while forgetting treason and impiety?

sentences.zh: 古人有雲，求忠臣必出孝子之門，卿母在城，不能顧之，何忠義之可望！

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: seeking a loyal minister must come from a filial son's gate; your mother is in the city, you cannot look after her—what loyalty and righteousness can be hoped!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said loyal ministers come only from filial homes. Your own mother remains inside these walls, yet you abandon her—what loyalty do you claim?

sentences.zh: 惡不絕世，卿之謂也。

translations.literal: Evil does not cut off generation—this is called of you.
translations.idiomatic: Villainy runs in families, as you prove.

sentences.zh: 不圖中州禮義之邦邦，而卿門風若斯。

translations.literal: I did not expect the Central Plain ritual-propriety state-state, yet your gate's wind is thus.
translations.idiomatic: I did not think to see such conduct in the heartland where ritual is law, yet your house sinks to this.

sentences.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！

translations.literal: You discard old mother like removing straw sandals—what more shall I discuss!
translations.idiomatic: You cast off your aged mother as you would a worn shoe—I waste breath on you.

sentences.zh: 」既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the city fell; Gun and Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: The city soon fell. Wang Gun and Fu Jian, Marquis of Gu'an, were both put to death by Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 丕復以王永為司徒、錄尚書事，徐義為尚書令，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Pi again appointed Wang Yong as Minister of Education, recording Masters of Writing affairs, Xu Yi as Director of the Masters of Writing, adding Grand Master of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi again named Wang Yong Minister of Education with oversight of the Masters of Writing, made Xu Yi Director of the Masters of Writing, and granted him the additional title Grand Master of the Right.

sentences.zh: 初，王廣還自成都也，奔其兄秦州刺史統。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Guang returned from Chengdu, he fled to his elder brother Wang Tong Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Guang withdrew from Chengdu, he fled to his brother Wang Tong, Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及長安不守，廣攻河州牧毛興於枹罕。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was not held, Guang attacked Shepherd of Hezhou Mao Xing at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, Wang Guang besieged Mao Xing, Governor of Hezhou, at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 興遣建節將軍、臨清柏衛平率其宗人千七百夜擊廣軍，大敗之。

translations.literal: Xing sent General Who Establishes Integrity, Baron Weiping of Linqing, leading his lineage kin one thousand seven hundred to night-attack Guang's army, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing dispatched Weiping, General Who Establishes Integrity and Baron of Linqing, with seventeen hundred clansmen in a night attack that routed Wang Guang's force.

sentences.zh: 王統復遣兵助廣，興於是嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Wang Tong again sent troops aiding Guang; Xing thereupon encircled the city firmly defending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong sent reinforcements to his brother, and Mao Xing withdrew behind the walls of Fuhan to endure a siege.

sentences.zh: 既而襲王廣，敗之，廣亡奔秦州，為隴西鮮卑匹蘭所執，送詣姚萇。

translations.literal: Afterward he raided Wang Guang, defeated him; Guang fled to Qinzhou, was seized by Longxi Xianbei Pilan, sent to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing then sortied, crushed Wang Guang, and drove him toward Qinzhou, where Xianbei tribesmen of Longxi under Pilan captured him and delivered him to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 興既敗王廣，謀伐王統，平上邽。

translations.literal: After Xing defeated Wang Guang, he plotted to attack Wang Tong and pacify Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Wang Guang, Mao Xing planned a campaign against Wang Tong to secure Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 袍罕諸氐皆窘於兵革而疲不堪命，乃殺興，推衛平為使持節、安西將軍、河州刺史，遣使請命。

translations.literal: The various Di of Paohan were all distressed by weapons and armor and weary, unable to bear commands; thereupon they killed Xing, promoted Wei Ping as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Hezhou, sent envoys requesting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Di clans of Fuhan were exhausted by endless war and could bear their orders no longer. They assassinated Mao Xing, acclaimed Wei Ping as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Hezhou, and sent envoys to seek recognition from the court.

sentences.zh: 刁雲殺慕容忠，乃推慕容永為使持節、大都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、雍、秦、梁、涼四州牧、錄尚書事、河東王、稱籓於垂。

translations.literal: Diao Yun killed Murong Zhong, thereupon promoted Murong Yong as Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Grand General, Great Chanyu, Shepherd of Yong, Qin, Liang, and Liang four provinces, recording Masters of Writing affairs, Prince of Hedong, declaring vassalage to Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yun murdered Murong Zhong and raised Murong Yong with the full panoply of titles—Bearer of the Staff, supreme commander, Grand General, Great Chanyu, governor of Yong, Qin, Liang, and Liang provinces, overseer of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Hedong—while acknowledging Murong Chui as overlord.

sentences.zh: 征東苻定、鎮東苻紹、征北苻謨、鎮北苻亮皆降于慕容垂。

translations.literal: Fu Ding who Campaigns East, Fu Shao who Garrisons East, Fu Mo who Campaigns North, Fu Liang who Garrisons North all surrendered to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang—the generals holding the east and north—all submitted to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 丕又進王永為左丞相，苻纂為大司馬，張蠔為太尉，王騰為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，徐義為司空，苻沖為車騎大將軍、尚書令、儀同三司，俱石子為衛大將軍、尚書左僕射，領官皆如故。

translations.literal: Pi again advanced Wang Yong as Left Chancellor, Fu Zuan as Grand Marshal, Zhang Hao as Grand Commandant, Wang Teng as Grand General of Agile Cavalry with ceremony equal to Three Dukes, Xu Yi as Minister of Works, Fu Chong as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Masters of Writing, ceremony equal to Three Dukes, Ju Shizi as Grand General Who Guards the Palace, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrent offices all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi promoted Wang Yong to Left Chancellor, Fu Zuan to Grand Marshal, Zhang Hao to Grand Commandant, Wang Teng to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with honors matching the Three Excellencies, Xu Yi to Minister of Works, Fu Chong to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director of the Masters of Writing with the same ceremonial rank, and Ju Shizi to Grand General Who Guards the Palace and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, while their other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永又檄州郡曰：「昔夏有窮夷之難，少康起焉；

translations.literal: Yong again called commanderies and prefectures, saying: "Formerly Xia had the Kiong Yi's calamity; Shaokang rose therefrom;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong issued another manifesto: "When the Xia dynasty faced the usurpation of Han Zhuo, Shaokang restored it;

sentences.zh: 王莽毒殺平帝，世祖重光漢道；

translations.literal: Wang Mang poison-killed Emperor Ping; the Shizu doubled brightness Han way;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang murdered the boy emperor Ping, yet Emperor Guangwu brought the Han back to light;

sentences.zh: 百六之運，何代無之！

translations.literal: The hundred-six's fortune—what age lacks it!
translations.idiomatic: Cycles of calamity visit every age—none is exempt.

sentences.zh: 天降喪亂，羌胡猾夏，先帝晏駕賊庭，京師鞠為戎穴，神州蕭條，生靈塗炭。

translations.literal: Heaven sent down mourning chaos; Qiang and Hu cunningly assaulted Xia; the late emperor expired in the bandit court; the capital region became entirely a barbarian den; divine land is desolate; living souls smeared in charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has sent disaster: Qiang and Hu ravage the heartland, our late sovereign met death in a rebel camp, the capital has become a lair of barbarians, and the Central Plain lies waste while the people burn in misery.

sentences.zh: 天未亡秦，社稷有奉。

translations.literal: Heaven has not yet destroyed Qin; the altars of soil and grain have one who serves.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has not withdrawn its mandate from Qin: the altars of state still have rightful guardians.

sentences.zh: 主上聖德恢弘，道侔光武，所在宅心，天人歸屬，必當隆中興之功，復配天之美。

translations.literal: The lord above's sagely virtue is vast and great; his way equals Guangwu; wherever he dwells in hearts, Heaven and men attach; he is sure to elevate middle revival's merit, restore matching Heaven's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign's virtue is boundless and his course rivals Emperor Guangwu's. Wherever he turns, men pledge their hearts; Heaven and humanity alike rally to him. He will surely complete a glorious restoration and again align the dynasty with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 姚萇殘虐，慕容垂凶暴，所過滅戶夷煙，毀發丘墓，毒遍存亡，痛纏幽顯，雖黃巾之害於九州，赤眉之暴于四海，方之未為甚也。

translations.literal: Yao Chang is cruel and violent; Murong Chui is fierce and brutal; where they pass they extinguish households and raze smoke, destroy and dig up tombs; poison spreads through the living and dead; pain coils hidden and manifest; though Yellow Turbans' harm on nine provinces, Red Eyebrows' violence on four seas, compared to them is not yet extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang is savage and Murong Chui ruthless: their armies erase villages to ash, break open tombs, and poison living and dead alike. Their cruelty outstrips even the Yellow Turbans or the Red Eyebrows bandits of old.

sentences.zh: 今素秋將及，行師令辰，公侯牧守，壘主鄉豪，或戮力國家，乃心王室，各率所統，以孟冬上旬會大駕于臨晉。

translations.literal: Now plain autumn will arrive; marching troops' auspicious hour; dukes, marquises, shepherds, guards, fort masters, township heroes—some join strength for the state, hearts set on the royal house—each lead what they command; in early winter's first ten days assemble the great chariot at Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn campaigns approach, and the season favors arms. Every noble, governor, garrison chief, and local leader who still loves the state must rally the forces under his command and rendezvous with the imperial host at Linjin during the first third of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 」於是天水姜延、馮翊寇明、河東王昭、新平張晏、京兆杜敏、扶風馬郎、建忠高平牧官都尉王敏等咸承檄起兵，各有眾數萬，遣使應丕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, Wang Min Jianzhong Gaoping pasture official commandant, and others all received the call and raised troops, each having hosts of several tens of thousands, sent envoys responding to Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, Wang Min, Commandant of Pasture Officials at Gaoping under the Jianzhong command, and others all mustered tens of thousands apiece in answer to the summons and sent envoys to Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 皆就拜將軍、郡守，封列侯。

translations.literal: All were thereupon appointed generals, commandery administrators, enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi confirmed each as general or prefect and invested them as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 冠軍鄧景擁眾五千據彭池，與竇沖為首尾，擊萇平涼太守金熙。

translations.literal: Deng Jing Champion General held five thousand hosts occupying Pengchi, with Dou Chong as head and tail, attacked Chang's Pingliang Administrator Jin Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jing, General Who Crowned the Army, led five thousand men in holding Pengchi, coordinated with Dou Chong in a pincers movement, and struck Jin Xi, Yao Chang's Administrator of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 安定北部都尉鮮卑沒奕於率鄯善王胡員吒、護羌中郎將梁苟奴等，與萇左將軍姚方成、鎮遠強京戰于孫丘谷，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Northern Commandant of Anding, the Xianbei Moyuyu, leading the King of Shanshan Hu Yuanzha, Liang Gounu General Who Protects the Qiang, and others, fought Yao Chang's General of the Left Yao Fangcheng and Qiang Jing who Stabilizes the Distance at Sunqiu Valley and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Moyuyu, the Xianbei Northern Commandant of Anding, led the king of Shanshan, Hu Yuanzha, Liang Gounu, General Who Protects the Qiang, and others against Yao Fangcheng, Yao Chang's general of the left, and Qiang Jing, General Who Stabilizes the Distance, at Sunqiu Valley and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 枹罕諸氐以衛平年老，不可以成事業，議廢之，而憚其宗強，連日不決。

translations.literal: The various Di of Fuhan, because Wei Ping was old in years and could not complete great enterprise, deliberated deposing him, yet feared his lineage was strong; for successive days they did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Di clans of Fuhan agreed that Wei Ping was too aged to lead yet hesitated to depose him, fearing the power of his clan, and for days they could reach no decision.

sentences.zh: 氐有啖青者，謂諸將曰：「大事宜定，東討姚萇，不可沈吟猶豫。

translations.literal: Among the Di was one Dan Qing, who said to the generals: "Great affairs ought to be settled; east to punish Yao Chang—cannot sink in hesitation and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: A Di leader named Dan Qing told the commanders: "We must settle leadership at once and march east against Yao Chang. This is no time for wavering.

sentences.zh: 一旦事發，反為人害。

translations.literal: Once the affair breaks out, on the contrary you become harmed by others.
translations.idiomatic: If word leaks before we act, we ourselves will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 諸軍但請衛公會儲眾將，青為諸軍決之。

translations.literal: The various armies only ask Duke Wei to assemble the stored host of generals; Qing will decide it for the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Duke Wei to a banquet with every commander present; I, Dan Qing, will settle the matter for you.

sentences.zh: 」眾以為然。

translations.literal: " The host deemed it right.
translations.idiomatic: The officers agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗諸將，青抽劍而前曰：「今天下大亂，豺狼塞路，吾曹今日可謂休戚是同，非賢明之主莫可濟艱難也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly feasted the generals; Qing drew his sword and stepped forward, saying: "Now all under Heaven is greatly chaotic; wolves block the roads; we today can be called sharing weal and woe; without a worthy and clear lord none can ford hardship.
translations.idiomatic: At the feast Dan Qing drew his sword and stepped forward. "The realm is in chaos and predators stalk every road. We share a single fate tonight, and only a worthy sovereign can see us through.

sentences.zh: 衛公朽耄，不足以成大事，宜反初服，以避賢路，狄道長苻登雖王室疏屬，而志略雄明，請共立之，以赴大駕。

translations.literal: Duke Wei is rotten and aged, not sufficient to complete great matters; ought to return to initial garments to yield the worthy road; Fu Deng Magistrate of Didao, though a distant kin of the royal house, yet in aspiration and strategy is heroic and clear—please together establish him, to go to the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wei is a spent old man unfit for leadership. Let him step aside in plain dress and clear the way for worthier men. Fu Deng, magistrate of Didao, is only a remote kinsman of the throne, yet he is bold and astute. I urge us to acclaim him and march to join the imperial host.

sentences.zh: 諸君若有不同者，便下異議。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen have those who differ, then set down opposing views.
translations.idiomatic: If any man disagrees, speak now—or hold your peace forever.

sentences.zh: 」乃奮劍攘袂，將斬貳己者，眾皆從之，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he brandished sword and pushed sleeves, about to behead those double-minded toward himself; the host all followed him; none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his blade and bared his arm as if to strike down any who wavered. Every officer submitted; none dared meet his eyes.

sentences.zh: 於是推登為帥，遣使於丕請命。

translations.literal: Thereupon they promoted Deng as commander, sent envoys to Pi requesting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They acclaimed Fu Deng as their leader and sent envoys to Fu Pi seeking imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 丕以登為征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、南安王、持節及州郡督因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Pi appointed Deng as Grand General Who Campaigns West, opening office with ceremony equal to Three Dukes, Prince of Nan'an, Bearer of the Staff, and prefectural and commandery supervisors according to what he styled and granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi named Fu Deng Grand General Who Campaigns West with independent headquarters and honors matching the Three Excellencies, Prince of Nan'an, and Bearer of the Staff; provincial and local commands were assigned to match the titles his followers already used.

sentences.zh: 又以徐義為右丞相。

translations.literal: He also appointed Xu Yi as Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi was appointed Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 丕留王騰守晉陽，楊輔戍壺關，率眾四萬進據平陽。

translations.literal: Pi left Wang Teng to defend Jinyang, Yang Fu to garrison Huguan, led a host of forty thousand forward to occupy Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi left Wang Teng to hold Jinyang and Yang Fu to guard Huguan while he marched forty thousand men into Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 王統以秦州降姚萇。

translations.literal: Wang Tong with Qinzhou surrendered to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong surrendered Qinzhou to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 慕容永以丕至平陽，恐不自固，乃遣使求假道還東，丕弗許。

translations.literal: Murong Yong because Pi arrived at Pingyang, feared not self-secure, therefore sent envoys requesting borrowed passage to return east; Pi did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong feared he could not hold his ground once Fu Pi reached Pingyang and asked for safe conduct eastward; Fu Pi refused.

sentences.zh: 遣王永及苻纂攻之，以俱石子為前鋒都督，與慕容永戰於襄陵。

translations.literal: He sent Wang Yong and Fu Zuan to attack him, appointing Ju Shizi as vanguard commander-in-chief, and fought Murong Yong at Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi dispatched Wang Yong and Fu Zuan against him, with Ju Shizi commanding the vanguard, and they met Murong Yong at Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 王永大敗，永及石子皆死之。

translations.literal: Wang Yong was greatly defeated; Yong and Shizi both died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong's army was routed; both Wang Yong and Ju Shizi fell in the battle.

sentences.zh: 初，苻纂之奔丕也，部下壯士三千餘人，丕猜而忌之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fu Zuan fled to Pi, his subordinates had more than three thousand stalwart warriors; Pi suspected and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Zuan first joined Fu Pi he brought three thousand picked fighters, and Fu Pi viewed him with jealousy and suspicion.

sentences.zh: 及永之敗，懼為纂所殺，率騎數千南奔東垣。

translations.literal: When Yong was defeated, he feared being killed by Zuan, led several thousand horsemen fleeing south to Dongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yong's defeat Fu Pi feared Fu Zuan might kill him and fled south to Dongyuan with several thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 晉揚威將軍馮該自陝要擊，敗之，斬丕首，執其太子甯、長樂王壽，送于京師，朝廷赦而不誅，歸之於苻宏。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Displays Might Feng Gai from Shan intercepted and attacked, defeated him, beheaded Pi's head, seized his Crown Prince Ning and Prince of Changle Shou, sent them to the capital; the court pardoned and did not execute, returned them to Fu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Gai, Eastern Jin's General Who Displays Might, ambushed him at Shan, broke his force, and beheaded Fu Pi. The crown prince Fu Ning and Fu Shou, Prince of Changle, were taken to the Jin capital, spared execution, and handed over to Fu Hong.

sentences.zh: 徐義為慕容永所獲，械埋其足，將殺之。

translations.literal: Xu Yi was captured by Murong Yong; shackles buried his feet; about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong captured Xu Yi, buried his legs in stocks, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 義誦《觀世音經》，至夜中，土開械脫，於重禁之中若有人導之者，遂奔楊佺期，佺期以為洛陽令。

translations.literal: Yi chanted the Guanshiyin Sutra; reaching midnight, earth opened and shackles came off; in heavy confinement as if someone guided him; thereupon he fled to Yang Quanqi; Quanqi appointed him Luoyang magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi recited the Avalokiteshvara scripture until, at midnight, the earth loosened and his fetters fell away. Though locked in the deepest prison, he seemed guided by an unseen hand. He escaped to Yang Quanqi, who named him magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 苻纂及弟師奴率丕余眾數萬，奔據杏城。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan and younger brother Shinu led Pi's remaining host of several tens of thousands, fled and held Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan and his brother Fu Shinu gathered tens of thousands of Fu Pi's survivors and withdrew to Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 苻登稱尊號，偽諡丕為哀平皇帝。

translations.literal: Fu Deng assumed the exalted title, falsely posthumously titled Pi as Emperor Aiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Deng took the throne he posthumously honored Fu Pi as Emperor Aiping of his own rump regime.

sentences.zh: 丕之臣佐皆沒慕容永，永乃進據上党之長子，僭稱大號，改元曰中興。

translations.literal: Pi's ministers and aides all fell to Murong Yong; Yong thereupon advanced to hold Zhangzi in Shangdang, usurped the great title, changed era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi's officials fell into Murong Yong's hands. Murong Yong then advanced to Zhangzi in Shangdang, declared himself emperor, and adopted the reign title Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 丕在位二年而敗。

translations.literal: Pi was on the throne two years and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi reigned only two years before ruin overtook him.

sentences.zh: 登字文高，堅之族孫也。

translations.literal: Deng, styled Wengao, was a lineage grandson of Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng, courtesy name Wengao, was a collateral descendant of Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 父敞，健之世為太尉司馬、隴東太守、建節將軍，後為苻生所殺。

translations.literal: Father Chang, in Jian's age was Grand Commandant's Major, Administrator of Longdong, General Who Establishes Integrity, afterward was killed by Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu Chang had served the founder Fu Jian (Emperor Jingming) as senior aide to the Grand Commandant, Administrator of Longdong, and General Who Establishes Integrity, until Fu Sheng put him to death.

sentences.zh: 堅即偽位，追贈右將軍、涼州刺史，以登兄同成嗣。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian assumed the usurped throne, he posthumously awarded Right General, Inspector of Liangzhou, and made Deng's elder brother Tongcheng heir.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian took the throne he posthumously honored Fu Chang as General of the Right and Inspector of Liangzhou, with Fu Deng's elder brother Fu Tongcheng continuing the line.

sentences.zh: 毛興之鎮上邽，以為長史。

translations.literal: When Mao Xing garrisoned Shanggui, he appointed him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Xing held Shanggui he named Fu Deng his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 登少而雄勇，有壯氣，粗險不修細行，故堅弗之奇也。

translations.literal: Deng from youth was heroic and brave, had stalwart qi, rough and perilous, did not cultivate small conduct; therefore Fu Jian did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Fu Deng was fierce and high-spirited but coarse and undisciplined, so Fu Jian never marked him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 長而折節謹厚，頗覽書傳。

translations.literal: Grown, he bent his measure, careful and thick, quite perused documents and traditions.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he curbed his temper, grew steady and conscientious, and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 拜殿上將軍，稍遷羽林監、揚武將軍、長安令，坐事黜為狄道長。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace General, gradually promoted to Commandant of the Feathered Forest, General Who Displays Might, Magistrate of Chang'an; sitting on an affair was demoted to Magistrate of Didao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Palace General to Commandant of the imperial guard, General Who Displays Might, and magistrate of Chang'an, then, after an offense, was reduced to magistrate of Didao.

sentences.zh: 及關中亂，去縣歸毛興。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was chaotic, he left the county and returned to Mao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong erupted in chaos he abandoned his post and joined Mao Xing.

sentences.zh: 同成言於興，請以登為司馬，常在營部。

translations.literal: Tongcheng spoke to Xing, requesting to appoint Deng as Marshal, always in camp headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tongcheng urged Mao Xing to commission Fu Deng as army marshal and keep him attached to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 登度量不群，好為奇略，同成常謂之曰：「汝聞不在其位，不謀其政，無數幹時，將為博識者不許。

translations.literal: Deng's measure was not of the herd; he liked to make strange stratagems; Tongcheng often said to him: "You have heard 'not in that office, do not plan that government'—without number interfering in the times, will be by broadly learned ones not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's judgment stood apart and he loved bold schemes. Fu Tongcheng often warned him: "You know the saying—hold no office, hatch no policy. Meddle once too often and learned men will condemn you.

sentences.zh: 吾非疾汝，恐或不喜人妄豫耳，自是可止。

translations.literal: I am not sick of you; I fear perhaps people do not like others rashly interfering—that from this can stop.
translations.idiomatic: I do not resent you, but others dislike unsolicited advice. From now on, curb yourself.

sentences.zh: 汝後得政，自可專意。

translations.literal: You afterward obtain government, naturally can devote intent.
translations.idiomatic: When power is truly yours, you may pursue your own course.

sentences.zh: 」時人聞同成言，多以為疾登而抑蔽之。

translations.literal: " People of the time hearing Tongcheng's words, mostly thought he resented Deng and suppressed and covered him.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners assumed Fu Tongcheng was jealous and was trying to silence Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登乃屏跡不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon screened traces and did not rashly associate.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng therefore kept a low profile and avoided casual company.

sentences.zh: 興有事則召之，戲謂之曰：「小司馬可坐評事。

translations.literal: When Xing had affairs then summoned him, jestingly said to him: "Little Marshal may sit judging affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mao Xing needed counsel he called him in and teased, "Let our junior marshal preside and settle the case.

sentences.zh: 」登出言輒析理中，興內服焉，然敬憚而不能委任。

translations.literal: " Deng's outgoing words always analyzed principle hitting the mark; Xing inwardly submitted, yet respected and feared and could not entrust office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's opinions invariably hit the mark. Mao Xing inwardly respected him yet never fully trusted him with power.

sentences.zh: 姚萇作亂，遣其弟碩德率眾伐毛興，相持久之。

translations.literal: Yao Chang made rebellion, sent his younger brother Shuode leading a host to attack Mao Xing; they stood off long.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang rebelled he sent his brother Yao Shuode against Mao Xing, and the two sides remained locked in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 興將死，告同成曰：「與卿累年共擊逆羌，事終不克，何恨之深！

translations.literal: Xing was about to die, told Tongcheng: "With you for accumulated years together striking the rebellious Qiang, the affair in the end did not succeed—how deep the regret!
translations.idiomatic: As Mao Xing lay dying he told Fu Tongcheng, "We spent years fighting the rebel Qiang and never broke them. My regret runs deep!

sentences.zh: 可以後事付卿小弟司馬，殄碩德者，必此人也。

translations.literal: You may entrust after-affairs to your younger brother the Marshal; the one who exterminates Shuode must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust what follows to your younger brother, our marshal—the man who will destroy Yao Shuode is he.

sentences.zh: 卿可換攝司馬事。」

translations.literal: You may exchange and act as Marshal affairs."
translations.idiomatic: You must step in and assume the marshal's office."

sentences.zh: 登既代衛平，遂專統征伐。

translations.literal: After Deng replaced Wei Ping, thereupon he solely commanded campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fu Deng succeeded Wei Ping he held sole command of military operations.

sentences.zh: 是時歲旱眾饑，道殣相望，登每戰殺賊，名為熟食，謂軍人曰：「汝等朝戰，幕便飽肉，何憂於饑！

translations.literal: At this time the year was drought and the host hungry; corpses on the road faced each other; Deng each battle killed bandits, named it cooked food, said to the soldiers: "You wait morning fight, evening then full meat—what worry about hunger!
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the land and the roads were lined with the dead. After every fight Fu Deng had the enemy dead cooked and told his men, "Fight at dawn and you feast on meat by dusk—why fear hunger?

sentences.zh: 」士眾從之，啖死人肉，輒飽健能鬥。

translations.literal: " Officers and host followed it, ate dead men's flesh, then were full, strong, able to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The troops obeyed, fed on human flesh, and grew strong and fierce in battle.

sentences.zh: 姚萇聞之，急召碩德曰：「汝不來，必為苻登所食盡。

translations.literal: Yao Chang heard it, urgently summoned Shuode: "If you do not come, surely will be by Fu Deng eaten up.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang heard this he urgently recalled Yao Shuode: "If you do not withdraw, Fu Deng's army will devour you to the last man.

sentences.zh: 」碩德於是下隴奔萇。

translations.literal: " Shuode thereupon descended Long and fled to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode then came down from the Long plateau and joined Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 及丕敗，丕尚書寇遺奉丕子渤海王懿、濟北王昶自杏城奔登。

translations.literal: When Pi was defeated, Pi's Minister Kou Yi bore Pi's sons Prince of Bohai Yi and Prince of Jibei Chang from Xingcheng fleeing to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Pi's fall his minister Kou Yi brought Fu Pi's sons Fu Yi, Prince of Bohai, and Fu Chang, Prince of Jibei, from Xingcheng to Fu Deng's camp.

sentences.zh: 登乃具丕死問，於是為丕發喪行服，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon fully had Pi's death inquiry; thereupon for Pi announced mourning and observed mourning garments; the three armies wore white.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng confirmed the news of Fu Pi's death, proclaimed mourning, and clothed the entire army in white.

sentences.zh: 登請立懿為主，眾咸曰：「渤海王雖先帝之子，然年在幼沖，未堪多難。

translations.literal: Deng requested establishing Yi as lord; the host all said: "Though the Prince of Bohai is the late emperor's son, yet his years are in young infancy, not able to bear many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng proposed enthroning Fu Yi, but the assembly replied, "The Prince of Bohai is the late emperor's son, yet he is only a child unfit to bear these calamities.

sentences.zh: 國亂而立長君，《春秋》之義也。

translations.literal: When the state is chaotic and establishes an elder lord—this is the Spring and Autumn's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that times of turmoil call for an adult ruler.

sentences.zh: 三虜跨僭，寇旅殷強，豺狼梟鏡，舉目而是，自厄運之極，莫甚於斯。

translations.literal: Three bandits stride usurpation; raider hosts abundant and strong; wolves and owl-mirrors, lifting eyes and thus it is; from misfortune's extreme, none exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Three usurpers divide the land, enemy hosts swarm like wolves and owls wherever we look—never has fate dealt the house of Fu a darker hour.

sentences.zh: 大王挺劍西州，鳳翔秦、隴，偏師暫接，姚萇奔潰，一戰之功，可謂光格天地。

translations.literal: Great king draws sword in western province, phoenix soars Qin and Long; partial army briefly engages, Yao Chang flees in rout; one battle's merit can be called light striking Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: You raised your sword in the western marches, swept Qin and Long like a soaring phoenix, and a single clash sent Yao Chang reeling—a feat whose brilliance fills heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 宜龍驤武奮，拯拔舊京，以社稷宗廟為先，不可顧曹臧、吳劄一介微節，以失圖運之機，不建中興之業也。

translations.literal: Ought dragon-soaring martial to rouse, save and pull old capital, take altars of soil and grain and ancestral temple as first; cannot heed Cao Zang, Wu Zha one petty integrity, thereby lose charting fortune's opportunity, not establish middle revival's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: You must march like a roused dragon, recover the old capital, and put the altars of state ahead of private scruple. Do not imitate Cao Zang or Wu Zha, who yielded throne for a minor point of honor, and forfeit the moment to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」登於是乙太元十一年僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元曰太初。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon in the eleventh year of Taiyuan usurped the emperor position, greatly pardoned within the realm, changed era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng therefore proclaimed himself emperor in the eleventh year of the Jin Taiyuan era, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Taichu.

sentences.zh: 立堅神主於軍中，載以輜軿，羽葆青蓋，車建黃旗，武賁之士三百人以衛之，將戰必告，凡欲所為，啟主而後行。

translations.literal: He established Fu Jian's spirit tablet in the army, carried in covered wagon, feather-canopy green cover, chariot raised yellow banner, three hundred martial Fen warriors to guard it; about to fight must announce; all desires to do, open to the lord then proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a spirit tablet for Fu Jian in the baggage train, shaded by kingfisher plumes and a green canopy, with yellow banners and three hundred picked guards. Before every battle he reported to the tablet and undertook no move without consulting it.

sentences.zh: 繕甲纂兵，將引師而東，乃告堅神主曰：「維曾孫皇帝臣登，乙太皇帝之靈恭踐寶位。

translations.literal: Repairing armor gathering weapons, about to lead the army east, then announced to Fu Jian's spirit tablet: "The great-grandson emperor subject Deng, before the Grand Emperor's spirit reverently treads the precious position.
translations.idiomatic: While arming for the eastern march he addressed Fu Jian's tablet: "Your great-grandson, Emperor Fu Deng, has ascended the throne in reverence before your august spirit.

sentences.zh: 昔五將之難，賊羌肆害於聖躬，實登之罪也。

translations.literal: Formerly at the Five Generals' calamity, the bandit Qiang wantonly harmed the sage person—truly Deng's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck the Five Garrisons, the Qiang rebels struck down your sacred person—that failure was mine.

sentences.zh: 今合義旅，眾余五萬，精甲勁兵，足以立功，年谷豐穰，足以資贍。

translations.literal: Now joining righteous hosts, the host exceeds fifty thousand; refined armor strong troops, sufficient to establish merit; year grain abundant, sufficient to supply provision.
translations.idiomatic: I now command more than fifty thousand loyal troops in stout armor, ample to win glory, and the harvests are rich enough to sustain them.

sentences.zh: 即日星言電邁，直造賊庭，奮不顧命，隕越為期，庶上報皇帝酷冤，下雪臣子大恥。

translations.literal: This day star-speech lightning dash, straight reach the bandit court, rouse not spare life, fall and cross as the term, hope above repay the emperor's bitter wrong, below wash ministers' and sons' great shame.
translations.idiomatic: This very day we march like shooting stars and lightning straight on the traitor's lair, ready to spend our lives if need be, that we may avenge your murder above and wipe away the shame of your servants below.

sentences.zh: 惟帝之靈，降監厥誠。

translations.literal: Only the emperor's spirit, descend and inspect this sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: May your spirit look down and witness my devotion.

sentences.zh: 」因覷欷流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sobbed and wept tears.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 將士莫不悲慟，皆刻鉾鎧為「死休」字，示以戰死為志。

translations.literal: Generals and soldiers none not grieved; all carved on spear armor the characters 'death rest', showing taking battle death as intent.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men wept with him and carved the words "death or rest" on their spears and armor, vowing to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 每戰以長槊鉤刃為方圓大陣，知有厚薄，從中分配，故人自為戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: Each battle used long lances hooked blades to make square-round great formation, knowing there is thick and thin, from middle distribute assign, therefore each man fought for himself, wherever faced none before.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he drew up massive formations of long spears and hooked blades, weighting the strong and weak wings so that every fighter knew his place. Each man fought as if for himself, and none could stand before them.

sentences.zh: 初，長安之將敗也，堅中壘將軍徐嵩、屯騎校尉胡空各聚眾五千，據險築堡以自固，而受姚萇官爵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang'an was about to be defeated, Fu Jian's Central Rampart General Xu Song and Cavalry Camp Commandant Hu Kong each gathered hosts of five thousand, held peril and built fortresses to secure themselves, yet received Yao Chang's offices and noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chang'an fell, Xu Song, Fu Jian's general of the central bastion, and Hu Kong, commandant of the mounted camp, each rallied five thousand men, fortified defensible heights, and even accepted titles from Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 及萇之害堅，嵩等以王禮葬堅於二堡之間。

translations.literal: When Chang harmed Fu Jian, Song and others with kingly rites buried Fu Jian between the two fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Chang murdered Fu Jian, Xu Song and his comrades buried him with royal ceremony between their two strongholds.

sentences.zh: 至是，各率眾降登。

translations.literal: By now, each led hosts surrendering to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: They now brought their forces over to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 拜嵩鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史，空輔國將軍、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He appointed Song General Who Garrisons the Army, Inspector of Yongzhou; Kong General Who Supports the State, Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Xu Song General Who Garrisons the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, and Hu Kong General Who Supports the State and governor of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 登復改葬堅以天子之禮。

translations.literal: Deng again changed burial of Fu Jian using Son of Heaven's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng reinterred Fu Jian with full imperial honors.

sentences.zh: 又僭立其妻毛氏為皇后，弟懿為皇太弟。

translations.literal: He also usurp-established his wife Lady Mao as empress, younger brother Yi as imperial younger brother heir.
translations.idiomatic: He named his wife Lady Mao empress and his younger brother Fu Yi heir presumptive as Prince Imperial Younger Brother.

sentences.zh: 遣使拜苻纂為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、太師，領大司馬，進封魯王，纂弟師奴為撫軍大將軍、并州牧、朔方公。

translations.literal: He sent envoys appointing Fu Zuan as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Marshal, advanced enfeoffment as Prince of Lu; Zuan's younger brother Shinu as Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Shepherd of Bingzhou, Duke of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys investing Fu Zuan with the staff, the palace post, supreme military command, the title Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Marshal, and princely rank in Lu, while Fu Shinu became Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Governor of Bingzhou, and Duke of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 纂怒謂使者曰：「渤海王世祖之孫，先帝之子，南安王何由不立而自尊乎？

translations.literal: Zuan angrily said to the envoy: "The Prince of Bohai is Shizu's grandson, the late emperor's son—how does the Prince of Nan'an come not to be established yet self-exalts?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan thundered at the envoy, "The Prince of Bohai is a grandson of Shizu and a son of the late emperor. By what right does the Prince of Nan'an seize the throne instead?

sentences.zh: 」纂長史王旅諫曰：「南安已立，理無中改。

translations.literal: " Zuan's Chief Clerk Wang Lü remonstrated: "Nan'an is already established; in principle there is no mid-change.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Wang Lü urged him, "Fu Deng is already enthroned; the deed cannot be undone midstream.

sentences.zh: 賊虜未平，不可宗室之中自為仇敵，原大王遠蹤光武推聖公之義，梟二虜之後，徐更圖之。

translations.literal: Bandit captives not yet pacified; cannot within the imperial clan make each other enemy foes; I beg great king track far Guangwu pushing Shengong's righteousness, behead the two captives afterward, slowly again plan it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still hold the field; the royal house cannot afford civil war. I beg you to follow Emperor Guangwu's example in deferring to Liu Xuan until the usurpers fell, then settle the succession.

sentences.zh: 」纂乃受命。

translations.literal: " Zuan thereupon received the command.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 於是貳縣虜帥彭沛谷、屠各董成、張龍世、新平羌雷惡地等盡應之，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Er county barbarian chiefs Peng Peigu, Tuge Dong Cheng, Zhang Longshi, Xinping Qiang Lei Edi and others all responded to him, having a host of more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders such as Peng Peigu of Er county, the Tuge chiefs Dong Cheng and Zhang Longshi, and the Xinping Qiang Lei Edi rallied to him with more than a hundred thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 纂遣師奴攻上郡羌酋金大黑、金洛生，大黑等逆戰，大敗之，斬首五千八百。

translations.literal: Zuan sent Shinu to attack Shangjun Qiang chiefs Jin Dahei, Jin Luosheng; Dahei and others resisted battle, greatly defeated them, beheaded five thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan sent Fu Shinu against the Qiang chieftains Jin Dahei and Jin Luosheng of Shangjun; they offered battle and were shattered, losing five thousand eight hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 登以竇沖為車騎大將軍、南秦州牧，楊定為大將軍、益州牧，楊璧為司空、梁州牧。

translations.literal: Deng appointed Dou Chong as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Shepherd of South Qinzhou; Yang Ding as Grand General, Shepherd of Yizhou; Yang Bi as Minister of Works, Shepherd of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Dou Chong Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Southern Qinzhou, Yang Ding Grand General and Governor of Yizhou, and Yang Bi Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻纂敗姚碩德于涇陽，姚萇自陰密距纂，纂退屯敷陸。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan defeated Yao Shuode at Jingyang; Yao Chang from Yinmi resisted Zuan; Zuan retreated to encamp at Fulu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan routed Yao Shuode at Jingyang until Yao Chang advanced from Yinmi to block him, forcing Fu Zuan back to Fulu.

sentences.zh: 竇沖攻萇汧、雍二城，克之，斬其將軍姚元平、張略等。

translations.literal: Dou Chong attacked Chang's Qian and Yong two cities, took them, beheaded their generals Yao Yuanping, Zhang Lüe and others.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong stormed Yao Chang's cities of Qian and Yong, captured them, and executed generals Yao Yuanping and Zhang Lüe among others.

sentences.zh: 又與萇戰於汧東，為萇所敗。

translations.literal: Again fought with Chang east of Qian, was defeated by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yao Chang again east of the Qian River and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 登次於瓦亭。

translations.literal: Deng halted at Wating.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng encamped at Wating.

sentences.zh: 萇攻彭沛穀堡，陷之，沛穀奔杏城，萇遷陰密。

translations.literal: Chang attacked Peng Peigu fortress, took it; Peigu fled to Xingcheng; Chang moved to Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang stormed Peng Peigu's stronghold, drove Peng Peigu to Xingcheng, and withdrew to Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 登征虜、馮翊太守蘭犢率眾二萬自頻陽入于和寧，與苻纂首尾，將圖長安。

translations.literal: Deng's Subduer of Captives, Lan Du Administrator of Fengyi, led a host of twenty thousand from Pinyang into Hening, with Fu Zuan head and tail, about to plan Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Du, Fu Deng's General Who Subdues Captives and Administrator of Fengyi, brought twenty thousand men from Pinyang into Hening to coordinate with Fu Zuan in a pincers aimed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 師奴勸其兄纂稱尊號，纂不從，乃殺纂，自立為秦公。

translations.literal: Shinu urged his elder brother Zuan to assume the exalted title; Zuan did not follow; thereupon he killed Zuan, self-established as Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shinu pressed his brother to claim the throne; when Fu Zuan refused, Fu Shinu murdered him and styled himself Duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 蘭犢絕之，皆為姚萇所敗。

translations.literal: Lan Du cut them off; all were defeated by Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Du broke with him, and both factions were crushed by Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登進所胡空堡，戎夏歸之者十有餘萬。

translations.literal: Deng advanced to Hukong fortress; Rong and Xia who attached to him were more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng advanced on Hukongbao, and more than a hundred thousand tribesmen and Chinese flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 姚萇遣其將軍姚方成攻陷徐嵩堡，嵩被殺，悉坑戎士。

translations.literal: Yao Chang sent his general Yao Fangcheng to attack and take Xu Song's fortress; Song was killed; all buried alive Rong soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Yao Fangcheng to storm Xu Song's fort; Xu Song died fighting and the garrison was buried alive.

sentences.zh: 登率眾下隴入朝那，姚萇據武都相持，累戰互有勝負。

translations.literal: Deng led the host down Long into Chaona; Yao Chang held Wudu standing off; repeated battles each had victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng descended from the Long plateau into Chaona while Yao Chang held Wudu; they clashed repeatedly with mixed results.

sentences.zh: 登軍中大饑，收葚以供兵士。

translations.literal: Deng's army inside greatly starved; gathered mulberries to supply soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped Fu Deng's camp, and the men fed on wild mulberries.

sentences.zh: 立其子崇為皇太子，弁為南安王，尚為北海王。

translations.literal: He established his son Chong as crown prince, Bian as Prince of Nan'an, Shang as Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Fu Chong crown prince, Fu Bian Prince of Nan'an, and Fu Shang Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 姚萇退還安定。

translations.literal: Yao Chang retreated returning to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang pulled back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 登就食新平，留其大軍于胡空堡，率騎萬餘圍萇營，四面大哭，哀聲動人。

translations.literal: Deng went to eat at Xinping, left his great army at Hukongbao, led more than ten thousand horsemen surrounding Chang's camp, four sides greatly weeping; mournful sound moved people.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng foraged in Xinping, left his main force at Hukongbao, and rode out with ten thousand horsemen to ring Yao Chang's camp, where his men wailed on every side until the sound of grief shook the enemy.

sentences.zh: 萇惡之，乃命三軍哭以應登，登乃引退。

translations.literal: Chang loathed it; thereupon ordered the three armies to weep to respond to Deng; Deng thereupon led retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, unnerved, ordered his own army to wail in answer, and Fu Deng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 萇以登頻戰輒勝，謂堅有神驗，亦于軍中立堅神主，請曰：「往年新平之禍，非萇之罪。

translations.literal: Chang because Deng frequently fought then won, said Fu Jian had spirit verification; also in the army established Fu Jian's spirit tablet, praying: "In former years Xinping's calamity was not Chang's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu Deng won battle after battle, Yao Chang concluded that Fu Jian's spirit was aiding him and set up a tablet to Fu Jian in his own camp, pleading, "The slaughter at Xinping years ago was not my doing.

sentences.zh: 臣兄襄從陝北渡，假路求西，狐死首丘，欲暫見鄉里。

translations.literal: Your subject's elder brother Xiang crossed from north of Shan, borrowed a road seeking west; the fox dies heading its hill—wished briefly to see his home village.
translations.idiomatic: My brother Yao Xiang crossed north of the Shan defile, begged passage to march west, and—like the fox that turns toward its native hill—only wanted a glimpse of his homeland.

sentences.zh: 陛下與苻眉要路距擊，不遂而沒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with Fu Mei at a choke point resisted and struck; did not succeed and perished.
translations.idiomatic: You and Fu Mei barred his path in battle, yet could not stop him and fell in the field.

sentences.zh: 襄敕臣行殺，非臣之罪。

translations.literal: Xiang ordered your subject to carry out the killing—it is not your subject's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang commanded me to strike the blow; the fault is not mine.

sentences.zh: 苻登陛下末族，尚欲復讎，臣為兄報恥，于情理何負！

translations.literal: Fu Deng is Your Majesty's terminal lineage, yet still wishes to take revenge; your subject for elder brother avenges shame—in feeling and principle what fault!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng is only a distant twig of your house, yet he burns to avenge you. I avenge my brother—where is the wrong in that?

sentences.zh: 昔陛下假臣龍驤之號，謂臣曰：'朕以龍驤建業，卿其勉之！

translations.literal: Formerly Your Majesty granted your servant the Dragon Soarer title, saying to your servant: 'I by Dragon Soarer established the enterprise—you should exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Once you bestowed on me the title General Dragon Soarer and said, 'It was as Dragon Soarer that I founded this realm—spare no effort!'

sentences.zh: '明詔昭然，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: 'The bright edict was clear; the words are still in the ears.
translations.idiomatic: That clear decree still rings in my ears.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖過世為神，豈假手於苻登而圖臣，忘前征時言邪！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has passed the age and become a spirit, how would you borrow Fu Deng's hand to plot against your servant—forgetting the words from the former expedition!
translations.idiomatic: Even as a spirit, would you truly work through Fu Deng to destroy me and forget what you said when we campaigned together?

sentences.zh: 今為陛下立神象，可歸休於此，勿計臣過，聽臣至誠。

translations.literal: Now for Your Majesty I erect a divine image; you may return and rest here; do not reckon your servant's faults; hear your servant's utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I have raised this effigy so your spirit may rest here. Pardon my faults and heed my heartfelt plea.

sentences.zh: 」登進師攻萇，既而升樓謂萇曰：「自古及今，安有殺君而反立神象請福，望有益乎！

translations.literal: " Deng advanced the army attacking Chang; afterward ascended a tower and said to Chang: "From antiquity to now, how can there be killing a lord yet in turn setting up a divine image seeking blessing—hope there is benefit!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng pressed his attack on Yao Chang, then mounted a tower and shouted, "Since time began, has any regicide set up an idol to beg blessings and expected it to help?

sentences.zh: 」大呼曰：「殺君賊姚萇出來，吾與汝決之，何為枉害無辜！

translations.literal: " He greatly called out: "Lord-killing bandit Yao Chang come out—I with you will decide it—why wrongly harm the guiltless!
translations.idiomatic: He roared, "Yao Chang, regicide, show yourself and face me in single combat! Why slaughter the innocent?

sentences.zh: 」萇憚而不應。

translations.literal: " Chang feared and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, unnerved, held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 萇自立堅神象，戰未有利，軍中每夜驚恐，乃嚴鼓斬象首以送登。

translations.literal: Chang himself set up Fu Jian's divine image; battle had not been favorable; the army each night was frightened; thereupon with strict drums beheaded the image's head to send to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's own effigy of Fu Jian brought no victory, and his camp suffered nightly panic until he had the image's head struck off with full fanfare and sent to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登將軍竇洛、竇於等謀反發覺，出奔於萇。

translations.literal: Deng's generals Dou Luo, Dou Yu and others plotted rebellion; discovered; fled out to Chang.
