translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's generals Dou Luo, Dou Yu, and others were caught plotting treason and fled to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登進討彭池不克，攻彌姐營及繁川諸堡，皆克之。

translations.literal: Deng advanced to punish Pengchi without success; attacked Mijie camp and the various fortresses of Fanchuan; all took them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng failed to take Pengchi but stormed the Mijie camp and every stronghold along Fanchuan, reducing them all.

sentences.zh: 萇連戰屢敗，乃遣其中軍姚崇襲大界，登引師要之，大敗崇于安丘，俘斬二萬五千，進攻萇將吳忠、唐匡於平涼，克之，以尚書苻碩原為前禁將軍、滅羌校尉，戍平涼。

translations.literal: Chang repeatedly fought repeatedly defeated; thereupon sent his central army Yao Chong to raid Dajie; Deng led the army to intercept, greatly defeated Chong at Anqiu, captured and beheaded twenty-five thousand; advanced to attack Chang's generals Wu Zhong and Tang Kuang at Pingliang, took them; appointed Minister Fu Shuoyuan as Forward Guard General, Colonel Who Extinguishes the Qiang, garrisoned Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: After a string of defeats Yao Chang sent Yao Chong to strike Dajie; Fu Deng intercepted him at Anqiu, annihilated twenty-five thousand men, then took Pingliang from Wu Zhong and Tang Kuang. He named Fu Shuoyuan of the Masters of Writing Forward Guard General and Colonel Who Extinguishes the Qiang to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 登進據苟頭原以逼安定。

translations.literal: Deng advanced to hold Goutouyuan to press Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng seized Goutouyuan and pressed against Anding.

sentences.zh: 萇率騎三萬夜襲大界營，陷之，殺登妻毛氏及其子弁、尚，擒名將數十人，驅掠男女五萬餘口而去。

translations.literal: Chang led thirty thousand horsemen night-raided Dajie camp, took it, killed Deng's wife Lady Mao and his sons Bian and Shang, seized several tens of famous generals, drove and plundered men and women more than fifty thousand mouths and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang led thirty thousand horsemen in a night assault on Dajie, slaughtered Fu Deng's wife Lady Mao and his sons Fu Bian and Fu Shang, captured dozens of noted commanders, and marched away more than fifty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 登收合餘兵，退據胡空堡，遣使齎書加竇沖大司馬、驃騎將軍、前鋒大都督、都督隴東諸軍事，楊定左丞相、上大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，楊璧大將軍、都督隴右諸軍事。

translations.literal: Deng gathered remaining troops, retreated to hold Hukongbao, sent envoys bearing documents promoting Dou Chong Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, Supervisor of Longdong Military Affairs; Yang Ding Left Chancellor, Supreme Grand General, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs; Yang Bi Grand General, Supervisor of Longyou Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng rallied his survivors at Hukongbao and sent orders elevating Dou Chong to Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, grand vanguard commander, and governor of Longdong; Yang Ding to Left Chancellor, supreme commander, and director of all military affairs; and Yang Bi to Grand General with authority over Longyou.

sentences.zh: 遣沖率見眾為先驅，自繁川趣長安。

translations.literal: He sent Chong leading the present host as vanguard, from Fanchuan hastening to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong was to lead the available forces as vanguard from Fanchuan toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 登率眾從新平逕據新豐之千戶固。

translations.literal: Deng led the host from Xinping straight to hold Xinfeng's Qianhugu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng marched from Xinping straight to the Qianhugu redoubt at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 使定率隴上諸軍為其後繼，璧留守仇池。

translations.literal: He ordered Ding to lead Longshang various armies as their rear follow-up; Bi remained guarding Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding would bring up the Longshang armies as rear guard while Yang Bi stayed to defend Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 又命其并州刺史楊政、冀州刺史楊楷率所統大會長安。

translations.literal: He also ordered his Inspector of Bingzhou Yang Zheng and Inspector of Jizhou Yang Kai to lead what they commanded to great assembly at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed Yang Zheng of Bingzhou and Yang Kai of Jizhou to march their commands to a general rendezvous at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 萇遣其將軍王破虜略地秦州，楊定及破虜戰于清水之格奴阪，大敗之。

translations.literal: Chang sent his general Wang Polu to seize land in Qinzhou; Yang Ding and Polu fought at Qingshui's Genu Slope, greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang dispatched Wang Polu to raid Qinzhou; Yang Ding met him at Genu Slope on the Qingshui River and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 登攻張龍世於鴦泉堡，姚萇救之，登引退。

translations.literal: Deng attacked Zhang Longshi at Yangquanbao; Yao Chang relieved him; Deng led retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng besieged Zhang Longshi at Yangquanbao until Yao Chang relieved the place, forcing Fu Deng to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 萇密遣其將任瓫、宗度詐為內應，遣使招登，許開門納之。

translations.literal: Chang secretly sent his generals Ren Kan, Zong Du feigning as inner responders, sent envoys summoning Deng, promised opening gates to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang secretly ordered Ren Kan and Zong Du to pose as defectors, sent messengers inviting Fu Deng in, and promised to open the gates.

sentences.zh: 登以為然。

translations.literal: Deng deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng believed them.

sentences.zh: 雷惡地馳謂登曰：「姚萇多計略，善御人，必為奸變，願深宜詳思。

translations.literal: Lei Edi galloped and said to Deng: "Yao Chang has many stratagems, is good at controlling men—surely will make treacherous change; wish deeply you should think in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Edi rode up to warn Fu Deng: "Yao Chang is cunning and commands men's loyalty; this will prove a trap. Think twice.

sentences.zh: 」登乃止。

translations.literal: " Deng thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng canceled the advance.

sentences.zh: 萇聞惡地之詣登也，謂諸將曰：「此羌多奸智，今其詣登，事必無成。

translations.literal: Chang heard Edi's going to Deng, said to the generals: "This Qiang has much treacherous wisdom; now his going to Deng, the affair surely will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang learned that Lei Edi had visited Fu Deng he told his officers, "That Qiang is full of guile; now that he has warned Fu Deng, the ruse is ruined.

sentences.zh: 」登聞萇懸門以待之，大驚，謂左右曰：「雷征東其殆聖乎！

translations.literal: " Deng heard Chang had raised the gate to await him, greatly startled, said to left and right: "Lei Who Campaigns East is perhaps nearly a sage!
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yao Chang had raised the portcullis to trap him, Fu Deng exclaimed to his staff, "General Lei Who Campaigns East must be almost a prophet!

sentences.zh: 微此公，朕幾為豎子所誤。

translations.literal: Without this lord, I nearly was misled by a stripling.
translations.idiomatic: Without him I would have walked into that boy's snare.

sentences.zh: 」萇攻陷新羅堡。

translations.literal: " Chang attacked and took Xinluobao.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang then stormed Xinluo fortress.

sentences.zh: 萇撫風太守齊益男奔登。

translations.literal: Chang's Fufeng Administrator Qi Yinan fled to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yinan, Administrator of Fufeng under Yao Chang, defected to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登將軍路柴、強武等並以眾降於萇。

translations.literal: Deng's generals Lu Chai, Qiang Wu and others all with hosts surrendered to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's generals Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and others brought their troops over to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登攻萇將張業生於隴東，萇救之，不克而退。

translations.literal: Deng attacked Chang's general Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Chang relieved him; did not succeed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng attacked Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Yao Chang tried to save him but failed and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 登將軍魏褐飛攻姚當成於杏城，為萇所殺。

translations.literal: Deng's general Wei Hefei attacked Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng, was killed by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hefei, Fu Deng's general, besieged Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and was slain by Yao Chang's forces.

sentences.zh: 馮翊郭質起兵廣鄉以應登，宣檄三輔曰：「義感君子，利動小人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhi of Fengyi raised troops at Guangxiang to respond to Deng, proclaimed to the Three Assistants: "Righteousness moves gentlemen; profit moves petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi of Fengyi rose at Guangxiang in support of Fu Deng and issued a manifesto to the capital region: "Honor moves the noble; gain moves the base.

sentences.zh: 吾等生逢先帝堯、舜之化，累世受恩，非常伯納言之子，即卿校牧守之胤，而可坐視豺狼忍害君父！

translations.literal: We are born encountering the late emperor's Yao-Shun transformation, accumulated generations receiving favor—we are either sons of changbo and remonstrance speakers, or heirs of ministers, colonels, shepherds, and guards—yet can sit watching wolves cruelly harm lord and father!
translations.idiomatic: We have lived under a sovereign as humane as Yao or Shun and received generations of grace. We are all sons of high ministers or heirs of governors—can we sit idle while jackals butcher our sovereign?

sentences.zh: 裸屍薦棘，痛結幽泉，山陵無松隧之兆，靈主無清廟之頌，賊臣莫大之甚，自古所未聞。

translations.literal: Naked corpse on thorns, pain knots the hidden spring; hills and tombs lack pine-tunnel omens; spirit lord lacks clear-temple hymns; treacherous minister none greater than this extreme—from antiquity never heard.
translations.idiomatic: His body was left naked among brambles; grief sinks to the yellow springs. No imperial mausoleum receives him, no hymn sounds in the clean temple. No traitor in history has outdone this—not in any age have we heard the like.

sentences.zh: 雖茹荼之苦，銜蓼之辛，何以諭之！

translations.literal: Though bitterwort's bitterness, holding smartweed's acridness—how with it to illustrate!
translations.idiomatic: Bitter herbs and biting wormwood cannot describe our pain!

sentences.zh: 姚萇窮凶肆害，毒被人神，於圖讖歷數萬無一分，而敢妄竊重名，厚顏瞬息，日月固所不照，二儀實亦不育。

translations.literal: Yao Chang exhausts viciousness and wanton harm, poison spreads to men and spirits; in charts and prophecies and celestial reckoning he lacks one ten-thousandth part, yet dares falsely steal weighty name, thick-faced in a breath—sun and moon solidly do not shine on him; the two principles in truth also do not nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's cruelty poisons heaven and earth, yet prophecy and celestial mandate grant him not the slightest legitimacy. Still he steals the imperial title without shame. The luminaries turn away; Heaven and Earth disown him.

sentences.zh: 皇天雖欲絕之，亦將假手於忠節。

translations.literal: August Heaven though wishing to cut him off, also will borrow hand from loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though High Heaven would destroy him, it will use the hands of the loyal to do it.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，皆夙漸神化，有懷義方，含恥而存，孰若蹈道而沒乎！

translations.literal: All hundred gentlemen, all long steeped in divine transformation, harbor righteous norms—holding shame yet surviving, how compares to treading the way and perishing!
translations.idiomatic: Every man of honor has imbibed the transforming power of the sages and keeps righteousness in his breast. Better to die for the right path than live shamed!

sentences.zh: 」眾咸然之。

translations.literal: " The host all deemed it right.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd roared assent.

sentences.zh: 唯鄭縣人苟曜不從，聚眾數千應姚萇。

translations.literal: Only Zhengxian man Gou Yao did not follow, gathered a host of several thousands responding to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gou Yao of Zheng county refused, raising several thousand men for Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登以質為平東將軍、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Deng appointed Zhi as General Who Pacifies the East, Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Guo Zhi General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 質遣部將伐曜，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Zhi sent a subordinate general to attack Yao, greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi sent a deputy against Gou Yao and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 質乃東引楊楷，以為聲援，又與曜戰于鄭東，為曜所敗，遂歸於萇，萇以為將軍。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon east drew Yang Kai as sounding aid, again fought Yao east of Zheng, was defeated by Yao, thereupon returned to Chang; Chang appointed him general.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi then called on Yang Kai in the east for support, fought Gou Yao again east of Zheng, lost, and submitted to Yao Chang, who made him a general.

sentences.zh: 質眾皆潰散。

translations.literal: Zhi's host all scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi's army melted away.

sentences.zh: 登自雍攻萇將金溫于范氏堡，克之，遂渡渭水，攻萇京兆太守韋范于段氏堡，不克，進據曲牢。

translations.literal: Deng from Yong attacked Chang's general Jin Wen at Fanshi Fortress, took it; thereupon crossed the Wei River, attacked Chang's Jingzhao Administrator Wei Fan at Duanshi Fortress, did not succeed; advanced to hold Qulao.
translations.idiomatic: From Yong Fu Deng took Jin Wen at Fanshi fortress, crossed the Wei, failed against Wei Fan at Duanshi fortress, and occupied Qulao.

sentences.zh: 苟曜有眾一萬，據逆方堡，密應登，登去曲牢繁川，次於馬頭願。

translations.literal: Gou Yao had a host of ten thousand, held Nifang Fortress, secretly responded to Deng; Deng left Qulao Fanchuan, halted at Matouyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao commanded ten thousand men at Nifang fortress and secretly aided Fu Deng, who moved from Qulao toward Fanchuan and camped at Matouyuan.

sentences.zh: 萇率騎來距，大戰敗之，斬其尚書吳忠，進攻新平。

translations.literal: Chang led horsemen coming to resist, great battle defeated him, beheaded his Minister Wu Zhong, advanced to attack Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang rode out to meet him, won a major victory, slew Minister Wu Zhong, and pressed on toward Xinping.

sentences.zh: 萇率眾救之，登引退，復攻安定，為萇所敗，據路承堡。

translations.literal: Chang led the host to relieve it; Deng led retreat; again attacked Anding, was defeated by Chang, held Lucheng Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang relieved the city; Fu Deng withdrew, struck Anding again, lost to Yao Chang, and fell back to Lucheng fortress.

sentences.zh: 是時萇疾病，見苻堅為崇。

translations.literal: At this time Chang was ill; saw Fu Jian as a haunting.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang fell ill and was haunted by visions of Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 登聞之，秣馬萬兵，告堅神主曰：「曾孫登自受任執戈，幾將一紀，未嘗不上天錫祐，皇鑒垂矜，所在必克，賊旅冰摧。

translations.literal: Deng heard it, fed horses ten thousand troops, announced to Fu Jian's spirit tablet: "Great-grandson Deng from receiving appointment holding spear, nearly will be one cycle of twelve years, never not up Heaven granting aid, imperial mirror hanging pity—wherever we go must conquer, bandit hosts ice-shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Fu Deng readied horse and men and addressed Fu Jian's tablet: "Your great-grandson has borne arms almost twelve years. Heaven has always blessed us; your spirit has shown pity. Every field is ours; rebel armies shatter like ice.

sentences.zh: 今太皇帝之靈降災疢於逆羌，以形類推之，醜虜必將不振。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Emperor's spirit sends sickness on the rebellious Qiang; by form-category inferring, the ugly captive surely will not rouse.
translations.idiomatic: Now your spirit has struck the traitor Qiang with illness; by every sign the wretch must fail.

sentences.zh: 登當因其隕斃，順行天誅，拯復梓宮，謝罪清廟。

translations.literal: Deng ought to ride his fall and death, follow and carry out Heaven's punishment, save and restore the catalpa palace coffin, apologize in guilt at the clear temple.
translations.idiomatic: I shall seize his dying moment to execute Heaven's judgment, recover your catafalque, and make amends before the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦境內，百僚進位二等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon greatly pardoned within the realm; hundred officials advanced rank two grades.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and promoted every official by two ranks.

sentences.zh: 與萇將姚崇爭麥于清水，累為崇所敗。

translations.literal: With Chang's general Yao Chong contested wheat at Qingshui, repeatedly was defeated by Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yao Chong for the wheat fields along the Qingshui and suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 進逼安定，去城九十餘里。

translations.literal: Advanced pressing Anding, distance from city more than ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to within ninety li of Anding.

sentences.zh: 萇疾小瘳，率眾距登，登去營逆萇，萇遣其將姚熙隆別攻登營，登懼，退還。

translations.literal: Chang's illness slightly healed, led the host resisting Deng; Deng left camp to meet Chang; Chang sent his general Yao Xilong separately to attack Deng's camp; Deng feared, retreated returning.
translations.idiomatic: As Yao Chang rallied, he marched against Fu Deng, who left camp to engage him. Yao Chang sent Yao Xilong against Fu Deng's rear; Fu Deng panicked and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 萇夜引軍過登營三十餘里以躡登後。

translations.literal: Chang night led the army past Deng's camp more than thirty li to tread on Deng's rear.
translations.idiomatic: By night Yao Chang slipped past Fu Deng's camp and swung more than thirty li onto his rear.

sentences.zh: 旦而候人告曰：「賊諸營已空，不知所向。

translations.literal: Dawn and the scout reported, saying: "The bandits' various camps are already empty; not known where they went.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn scouts reported, "The enemy camps stand empty; we cannot tell where they went.

sentences.zh: 」登驚曰：「此為何人，去令我不知，來令我不覺，謂其將死，忽然復來，朕與此羌同世，何其厄哉！

translations.literal: " Deng startled said: "What manner of man is this—going makes me not know, coming makes me not sense; said he was about to die, suddenly comes again—I with this Qiang share the age—how bitter!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng cried, "What sort of foe vanishes without trace, returns unseen, plays at death yet strikes again? To share an age with this Qiang—what curse is this?

sentences.zh: 」遂罷師還雍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon dismissed the army returning to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He broke off the campaign and withdrew to Yong.

sentences.zh: 以竇沖為右丞相。

translations.literal: He appointed Dou Chong as Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong was named Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 尋而沖叛，自稱秦王，建年號。

translations.literal: Soon Chong rebelled, styled himself Prince of Qin, established era name.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dou Chong rebelled, declared himself King of Qin, and adopted a reign title.

sentences.zh: 登攻之於野人堡，沖請救于姚萇，萇遣其太子興攻胡空堡以救之。

translations.literal: Deng attacked him at Yerengbao; Chong requested aid from Yao Chang; Chang sent his heir apparent Xing to attack Hukongbao to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng besieged him at Yereng fortress. Dou Chong begged Yao Chang for help, and Yao Chang sent the crown prince Yao Xing against Hukongbao to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 登引兵還赴胡空堡，沖遂與萇連和。

translations.literal: Deng led troops returning to rush to Hukongbao; Chong thereupon with Chang joined peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng wheeled back toward Hukongbao, and Dou Chong made common cause with Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 至是萇死，登聞之喜曰：「姚興小兒，吾將折杖以笞之。

translations.literal: By now Chang died; Deng heard it and joyfully said: "Yao Xing little child—I will break a rod to flog him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang died, Fu Deng exulted, "Yao Xing is a mere boy; I will break a switch to whip him with.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，盡眾而東，攻屠各姚奴、帛蒲二堡，克之，自甘泉向關中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon great pardon, entire host east, attacked Tuge Yao Nu and Bopu two fortresses, took them, from Ganquan toward Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed amnesty, marched the whole army east, stormed the Tuge strongholds of Yao Nu and Bopu, and advanced from Ganquan into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興追登不及數十里，登從六陌趣廢橋，興將尹緯據橋以待之。

translations.literal: Xing pursued Deng not reaching several tens of li; Deng from Liumo hastened to Feiqiao; Xing's general Yin Wei held the bridge awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing pursued but remained tens of li behind as Fu Deng hurried from Liumo toward Feiqiao, where Yin Wei held the bridge against him.

sentences.zh: 登爭水不得，眾渴死者十二三。

translations.literal: Deng contested water without obtaining; the host thirsty-dead were two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng could not win the watering places, and two or three men in ten died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 與緯大戰，為緯所敗，其夜眾潰，登單馬奔雍。

translations.literal: With Wei great battle, was defeated by Wei; that night the host broke; Deng single horse fled to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yin Wei and lost; that night his army collapsed, and Fu Deng fled alone on horseback to Yong.

sentences.zh: 初，登之東也，留其弟司徒廣守雍，太子崇守胡空堡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Deng went east, he left his younger brother Minister of Education Guang guarding Yong, Crown Prince Chong guarding Hukongbao.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Deng marched east he had left his brother Fu Guang, Minister of Education, at Yong and the crown prince Fu Chong at Hukongbao.

sentences.zh: 廣、崇聞登敗，出奔，眾散。

translations.literal: Guang and Chong heard Deng was defeated, fled out, host scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard of Fu Deng's defeat, Fu Guang and Fu Chong fled and their troops dispersed.

sentences.zh: 登至，無所歸，遂奔平涼，收集遺眾入馬毛山。

translations.literal: Deng arrived, had nowhere to return, thereupon fled to Pingliang, gathered remnant host entering Maomaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng found no refuge and raced to Pingliang, where he gathered survivors and withdrew into the Maomao Hills.

sentences.zh: 興率眾攻之，登遣子汝陰王宗質於隴西鮮卑乞伏乾歸，結婚請援，乾歸遣騎二萬救登。

translations.literal: Xing led the host attacking him; Deng sent son Prince of Ruyin Zong as hostage to Longxi Xianbei Qifu Gangui, allied marriage requesting aid; Gangui sent twenty thousand horsemen to relieve Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing attacked him there. Fu Deng sent his son Fu Zong, Prince of Ruyin, as hostage to the Xianbei chief Qifu Gangui of Longxi, sealed the tie with a marriage alliance, and begged rescue. Qifu Gangui sent twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 登引軍出迎，與興戰于山南，為興所敗，登被殺。

translations.literal: Deng led the army out to welcome, fought Xing south of the mountain, was defeated by Xing, Deng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng marched out to meet them, fought Yao Xing south of the mountains, was defeated, and was slain.

sentences.zh: 在位九年，時年五十二。

translations.literal: On the throne nine years; at the time age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned nine years and was fifty-two when he died.

sentences.zh: 崇奔於湟中，僭稱尊號，改元延初。

translations.literal: Chong fled to Huangzhong, usurped assuming exalted title, changed era to Yanchu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong fled to the Huangshui valley, declared himself emperor, and adopted the reign title Yanchu.

sentences.zh: 偽諡登曰高皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: False posthumous titled Deng as Emperor Gao, temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: His court posthumously named him Emperor Gao with temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 崇為乾歸所逐，崇、定皆死。

translations.literal: Chong was driven by Gangui; Chong, Ding both died.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui drove out Fu Chong; both Fu Chong and Yang Ding perished.

sentences.zh: 始，健以穆帝永和七年僭立，至登五世，凡四十有四歲，以孝武帝太元十九年滅。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Jian in Emperor Mu's Yonghe seventh year usurped established; reaching Deng five generations; altogether forty-four years; in Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan nineteenth year destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: From Fu Jian's usurpation in the seventh year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin through five generations to Fu Deng, the state lasted forty-four years and fell in the nineteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 索泮，字德林，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Pan, styled Delin, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan, courtesy name Delin, was a native of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 世為冠族。

translations.literal: Generation after generation were cap-gentry clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been eminent for generations.

sentences.zh: 泮少時遊俠，及長，變節好學，有佐世才器。

translations.literal: Pan in youth was wandering knight-errant; grown, changed measure fond of learning, had aiding-the-age talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he roamed as a knight-errant; as an adult he reformed, took to scholarship, and showed the makings of a statesman.

sentences.zh: 張天錫輔政，以泮為冠軍、記室參軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi assisted government, appointed Pan as Champion and secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Tianxi directed affairs he named Suo Pan General Who Crowned the Army and aide in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天錫即位，拜司兵，歷位禁中錄事。

translations.literal: Tianxi ascended the throne, appointed Director of Soldiers, passed through posts as palace recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Tianxi took the throne Suo Pan became Director of Military Affairs and served as recorder within the palace.

sentences.zh: 執法禦掾，州府肅然，郡縣改跡。

translations.literal: Holding law as controlling aide, prefecture and headquarters were austere; commanderies and counties changed tracks.
translations.idiomatic: As judicial supervisor he brought order to the provincial yamen and reformed conduct in every county.

sentences.zh: 遷羽林左監，有勤幹之稱。

translations.literal: Promoted to Left Commandant of the Feathered Forest; had diligent-capable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left commandant of the imperial guard, he earned a name for diligence and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 出為中壘將軍、西郡武威太守、典戎校尉。

translations.literal: Went out as Central Rampart General, Xijun Wuwei Administrator, Colonel Director of Military Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as general of the central bastion, Administrator of Wuwei in Xijun, and colonel in charge of tribal troops.

sentences.zh: 政務寬和，戎夏懷其惠，天錫甚敬之。

translations.literal: Government affairs were lenient and harmonious; Rong and Xia cherished his kindness; Tianxi greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild and just; tribesmen and Chinese alike cherished his kindness, and Zhang Tianxi held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 苻堅見而歎曰：「涼州信多君子！

translations.literal: Fu Jian saw and sighed, saying: "Liangzhou truly has many gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian met him and marveled, "Liangzhou truly breeds gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 」既而以泮河西德望，拜別駕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon because Pan's Hexi virtue and renown, appointed aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: For his moral stature on the western frontier Suo Pan was named chief administrator of the province.

sentences.zh: 呂光既克姑臧，泮固郡不降，光攻而獲之。

translations.literal: After Lü Guang had taken Guzang, Pan firmly held the commandery not surrendering; Guang attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang seized Guzang, Suo Pan held his commandery until Lü Guang stormed it and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「孤既平西域，將赴難京師，梁熙無狀，絕孤歸路，此朝延之罪人，卿何意阻郡固迷，自同元惡！

translations.literal: Guang said: "I have already pacified the Western Regions, about to go to the capital's distress; Liang Xi without form cut off my return road—this court-extension's criminal—what intention do you have blocking the commandery stubbornly deluded, making yourself the same as the chief villain!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, "I have pacified the west and mean to rescue the capital. Liang Xi blocked my road home like a traitor to the court. Why do you cling to your district like him and rank yourself among the arch-villains?

sentences.zh: 」泮厲色責光曰：「將軍受詔討叛胡，可受詔亂涼州邪？

translations.literal: " Pan with stern countenance rebuked Guang: "The general received edict to punish rebellious Hu—can you receive edict to throw Liangzhou into chaos?
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan answered sharply, "You were ordered to chastise rebel Hu—were you ordered to ravage Liangzhou?

sentences.zh: 寡君何罪，而將軍害之？

translations.literal: What crime had our lord, yet the general harmed him?
translations.idiomatic: What crime had our prince committed that you should destroy him?

sentences.zh: 泮但苦力寡，不能固守以報君父之讎，豈如逆氐彭濟望風反叛！

translations.literal: Pan only bitterly strength was scant, could not firmly guard to avenge lord-father's foe—how like the rebellious Di Peng Ji who at wind's sight rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: I regret only my weakness, which kept me from holding long enough to avenge my sovereign. Am I to be compared with Peng Ji of the Di, who betrayed his lord at the first rumor?

sentences.zh: 主滅臣死，禮之常也。

translations.literal: Lord perishes, minister dies—this is ritual's constant.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign falls, his minister dies with him—that is the constant teaching of propriety.

sentences.zh: 」乃就刑於市，神色不變。

translations.literal: " Thereupon went to execution in the market; spirit and countenance did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the public scaffold unflinching.

sentences.zh: 弟菱，有俊才，仕張天錫為執法中郎、冗從右監。

translations.literal: Younger brother Ling had outstanding talent; served Zhang Tianxi as Law-Enforcement Gentleman and Supernumerary Right Overseer.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Suo Ling was a brilliant man who served Zhang Tianxi as director of law enforcement and supernumerary overseer of the right.

sentences.zh: 苻堅世至伏波將軍、典農都尉，與泮俱被害。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's age reached General Who Calms the Waves, Commandant of Agriculture, and with Pan together was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he rose to General Who Calms the Waves and commandant of agriculture; he perished together with Suo Pan.

sentences.zh: 徐嵩，字元高，盛之子也。

translations.literal: Xu Song, styled Yuangao, was Sheng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Song, courtesy name Yuangao, was the son of Xu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 少以清白著稱。

translations.literal: From youth by pure integrity was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he was known for spotless integrity.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時舉賢良，為郎中，稍遷長安令，貴戚子弟犯法者，嵩一皆考竟，請托路絕。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time was recommended worthy and good, became Palace Gentleman, gradually promoted to Magistrate of Chang'an; noble in-law sons and younger kin who violated the law—Song in every case investigated to the end; request-and-entreaty roads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he was nominated as a worthy candidate, served as a court gentleman, and rose to magistrate of Chang'an. He prosecuted every lawbreaking kinsman of the great houses without fear, and influence-peddling at his yamen ceased.

sentences.zh: 堅甚奇之，謂其叔父成曰：「人為長吏，故當應耳。

translations.literal: Fu Jian greatly marveled at him, said to his uncle Cheng: "Others become senior officials, therefore ought to comply—that's all.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was deeply impressed and told Xu Song's uncle Xu Cheng, "Most men take high office merely to go through the motions.

sentences.zh: 此年少落落，有端貳之才。

translations.literal: This youth is lofty and detached; has talent fit for deputy excellence.
translations.idiomatic: This young man stands apart; he has the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」遷守始平郡，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: " Promoted to guard Shiping commandery; greatly had awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shiping, where he ruled with both authority and kindness.

sentences.zh: 及壘陷，姚方成執而數之，嵩厲色謂方成曰：「汝姚萇罪應萬死，主上止黃眉之斬而宥之，叨據內外，位為列將，無犬馬識養之誠，首為大逆。

translations.literal: When the rampart fell, Yao Fangcheng seized him and rebuked him; Song with stern countenance said to Fangcheng: "Your Yao Chang's crime deserved ten thousand deaths; the sovereign stayed Huangmei's beheading and pardoned him; he presumptuously occupied inside and outside, rank as arrayed general, lacked dog-and-horse knowing-nurture sincerity, first enacted great treason.
translations.idiomatic: When the fortress fell Yao Fangcheng seized him for interrogation. Xu Song thundered, "Yao Chang deserved death a thousand times over, yet our sovereign stayed the execution his captors demanded and spared him. He rose to general's rank yet showed none of a hound's loyalty to its master and became the first to rebel.

sentences.zh: 汝曹羌輩豈可以人理期也！

translations.literal: You lot Qiang ilk—how can human principle be expected!
translations.idiomatic: How can one expect human decency from you Qiang?

sentences.zh: 何不速殺我，早見先帝，取姚萇於地下。

translations.literal: Why not quickly kill me, early see the former emperor, seize Yao Chang under the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now that I may join the late emperor and drag Yao Chang down to justice beneath the earth.

sentences.zh: 」方成怒，三斬嵩，漆其首為便器。

translations.literal: " Fangcheng angry, thrice beheaded Song, lacquered his head as a urinal vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yao Fangcheng had him cut in three and lacquered his skull into a chamber pot.

sentences.zh: 登哭之哀慟，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Deng wept for him in bitter grief, posthumously awarded Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, ceremony equal to Three Dukes, posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng mourned him bitterly and posthumously named him Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors matching the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous epithet Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自兩京殄覆，九土分崩，赤縣成蛇豕之墟，紫宸遷蛙黽之穴，干戈日用，戰爭方興，猶逐鹿之並驅，若瞻烏之靡定。

translations.literal: The historian says: From the two capitals' extinction and overthrow, the nine soils split and collapsed; the Red County became snake-and-boar ruins; the Purple Palace moved to frog-and-toad dens; shields and spears daily used, war just rising—like chasing the deer with parallel gallop, like gazing at crows without settling.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: After the twin capitals fell and the realm shattered, the heartland became a wasteland of serpents and swine, the throne a burrow for frogs and newts. Arms clashed daily as war spread—all pursued the deer together, none knew where the crow would next alight.

sentences.zh: 苻洪擅蠻陬之桀黠，乘羯虜之危亡，乃附款江東而志圖關右，禍生蠆毒，未逞狼心。

translations.literal: Fu Hong monopolized the savage borderlands' fierce cunning, rode the Jie captives' peril and death; thereupon attached allegiance east of the River while intent on plotting Guan-you; calamity arose from scorpion venom; did not yet display wolf heart.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong wielded the fierce cunning of the southern tribes and exploited the Jie in their death throes. He pledged fealty to the court east of the Yangzi even as he schemed to take the northwest. Poison struck before his wolfish ambition could fully show.

sentences.zh: 健既承家，克隆凶緒，率思歸之眾，投山西之隙，據億丈之岩險，總三秦之果銳，敢窺大寶，遂竊鴻名，校數奸雄，有可言矣。

translations.literal: Jian having inherited the house, was able to enlarge the vicious thread, led homesick hosts, cast into Shanxi's crack, held billion-zhang cliff peril, commanded three Qin's resolute sharpness, dared to peer at the great treasure, thereupon stole the great name—reckoning and counting treacherous heroes, there is what can be said.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian inherited that legacy, magnified its violent course, led homesick armies through the opening west of the mountains, seized precipitous strongholds, and concentrated the fiercest fighters of the three Qins. He dared covet the throne and usurp a grand title—among the age's usurpers he merits mention.

sentences.zh: 長生慘虐，稟自率由。

translations.literal: Changsheng cruel and violent, received from following self.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng, styled Changsheng, was wantonly cruel by innate disposition.

sentences.zh: 睹辰象之災，謂法星之夜飲；

translations.literal: Seeing the celestial signs' calamity, called it the law-star's night drinking;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing portents in the stars, he called them the planet of law carousing at night;

sentences.zh: 忍生靈之命，疑猛獸之朝饑。

translations.literal: Bearing with living souls' fates, suspected fierce beasts' morning hunger.
translations.idiomatic: he toyed with the lives of the people as if wondering whether a beast were hungry at dawn.

sentences.zh: 但肆毒于刑殘，曾無心於戒懼。

translations.literal: Only wantoned poison in punishments and mutilation; never had heart for caution and fear.
translations.idiomatic: He reveled in torture and mutilation and never thought of restraint.

sentences.zh: 招亂速禍，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: Summoning chaos hastening calamity—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder he brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 永固雅量瑰姿，變夷眾夏，葉魚龍之謠詠，挺草付之休征，克翦奸回，纂承偽曆，遵明王之德教，闡先聖之儒風，撫育黎元，憂勤庶政。

translations.literal: Yonggu had capacious measure and rare bearing, transformed Yi and gathered Xia, harmonized fish-dragon ballads and songs, displayed grass-Fu's auspicious omen, was able to cut wicked and devious, continued and received usurped calendar, followed bright kings' virtue-teaching, expounded former sages' Confucian wind, nurtured black-haired people, worried and diligent in myriad government.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, styled Yonggu, combined dignity and presence, won over barbarian and Chinese alike, fulfilled the fish-into-dragon prophecies and the omen of the character Fu in the reed, purged traitors, seized the usurped mandate, promoted humane government, revived Confucian learning, cherished the common people, and toiled at every duty of state.

sentences.zh: 王猛以宏材緯軍國，苻融以懿戚贊經綸，權薛以諒直進規謨，鄧、張以忠勇恢威略，俊賢效足，杞梓呈才，文武兼施，德刑具舉。

translations.literal: Wang Meng by great talent wove army and state; Fu Rong by imperial kin assisted planning; Quan and Xue by candid straightness advanced regulations and plans; Deng and Zhang by loyalty and courage expanded might and strategy; outstanding worthies offered footwork, catalpa and zelkova displayed talent; civil and martial both applied; virtue and punishment both raised.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng shaped army and realm with grand ability; Fu Rong, as kinsman, helped steer policy; Quan and Xue offered blunt counsel; Deng and Zhang widened the empire through loyalty and valor. Talents flocked like fine timber in a forest; civil and military measures worked in tandem, kindness and law alike enforced.

sentences.zh: 乃平燕定蜀，擒代吞涼，跨三分之二，居九州之七，遐荒慕義，幽險宅心，因止馬而獻歌，托棲鸞以成頌，因以功侔曩烈，豈直化洽當年！

translations.literal: Thereupon pacified Yan, settled Shu, captured Dai, swallowed Liang, straddled two-thirds, occupied seven of nine provinces; distant wastes admired righteousness, hidden peril lodged hearts; therefore halting horses presented songs, lodging roosting phoenixes to complete hymns; thereby merit matched former fierce deeds—how only transformation harmonized the present year!
translations.idiomatic: He subdued Yan, secured Shu, seized Dai, absorbed Liang, held two-thirds of the realm and seven of the nine provinces. Far lands offered allegiance; wild regions bent the knee. Hymns hailed him beside halted steeds; odes compared him to nesting phoenixes. His achievements rivaled the ancient conquerors—his sway was not merely a moment's peace.

sentences.zh: 雖五胡之盛，莫之比也。

translations.literal: Though the Five Hu's flourishing, none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Even among the mightiest of the Five Hu, none matched him.

sentences.zh: 既而足己誇世，愎諫違謀，輕敵怒鄰，窮兵黷武。

translations.literal: Afterward self-satisfied boasting to the world, stubbornly rejecting remonstrance and opposing counsel, slighting enemies and enraging neighbors, exhausting troops and abusing arms.
translations.idiomatic: Then he grew complacent, spurned good counsel, despised his foes and provoked his neighbors, and exhausted the realm in ceaseless war.

sentences.zh: 懟三正之未葉，恥五運之猶乖，傾率土之師，起滔天之寇，負其犬羊之力，肆其吞噬之能。

translations.literal: Resenting the three rectifications' not aligning, shaming the five cycles' still awry, tilted the whole realm's hosts, raised flooding-Heaven's bandits, relied on dog-and-sheep strength, wantoned swallowing-devouring ability.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful that heaven's mandate had not settled in his favor, ashamed that the five phases had not turned his way, he hurled every soldier of the empire against a foe that blotted out the sky, trusting brute force and the appetite of a wolf.

sentences.zh: 自謂戰必勝，攻必取，便欲鳴鸞禹穴，駐蹕疑山，疏爵以侯楚材，築館以須歸命。

translations.literal: Self-deemed battle must win, attack must take, then wished to sound simurgh at Yu's cave, halt imperial progress at Yi Mountain, spread noble ranks to enfeoff Chu talents, build lodges to await surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Certain every battle would be victory, he dreamed of halting his chariot at Yu's shrine and the Marchmount of the Nine Doubts, enfeoffing Jin's worthies and building guest halls for a conquered court's surrender.

sentences.zh: 曾弗知人道助順，神理害盈，雖矜涿野之強，終致昆陽之敗。

translations.literal: Never knew human way aids compliance, divine pattern harms excess; though boasting Zhuoye's strength, in the end brought Kunyang's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He did not see that heaven favors the righteous and cuts down the proud: however mighty he thought himself at Zhuolu, he met the shame of Kunyang.

sentences.zh: 遂使凶渠候隙，狡寇伺間，步搖啟其禍先，燒當乘其亂極，宗社遷於他族，身首罄於賊臣，貽戒將來，取笑天下，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Thereupon caused fierce chieftains to watch for cracks, cunning bandits to spy for gaps; Buyao opened their calamity's start; Shao Dang rode their chaos's extreme; ancestral altars moved to other clans; body and head exhausted on traitor ministers—leaving warning for the future, inviting laughter under Heaven—is it not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Villains watched for weakness; rebels seized their chance. The Buyao struck first; the Shao Dang tribes finished the ruin. The altars passed to strangers; his body was broken by traitors—a warning to posterity and a jest to the world. What grief!

sentences.zh: 豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: Is it not erroneous!
translations.idiomatic: How profound his folly!

sentences.zh: 苻丕承亂僭竊，尋及傾敗，斯可謂天之所廢，人不能支。

translations.literal: Fu Pi inherited chaos and usurp-stole; soon reached overturn and defeat—this can be called what Heaven casts off, men cannot support.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi seized a throne amid chaos and soon collapsed—truly what Heaven abandons no man can uphold.

sentences.zh: 苻登集離散之兵，厲死休之志，雖眾寡不敵，難以立功，而義烈慷慨，有足稱矣。

translations.literal: Fu Deng gathered scattered troops, sharpened death-rest intent; though many-few did not match, hard to establish merit, yet righteous ardor was stirring—there is enough to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng rallied broken armies and forged them with a vow to fight to the death. Though outnumbered and unable to win lasting success, his fervor and honor deserve remembrance.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：洪惟壯勇，威棱氐種。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Hong was mighty and brave; awe and edge over the Di race.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Fu Hong was bold and fierce; his might awed the Di.

sentences.zh: 健藉世資，遂雄關、隴。

translations.literal: Jian relied on age's capital; thereupon was heroic over Pass and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian drew on that inheritance and made himself master of the pass and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 長生昏虐，敗不旋踵。

translations.literal: Changsheng benighted and cruel; defeat did not turn heel.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng ruled in brutish darkness and fell before he could turn around.

sentences.zh: 永固禎祥，肇自龍驤。

translations.literal: Yonggu's auspicious omens began from Dragon Soarer.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's good fortune began when he bore the title Dragon Soarer.

sentences.zh: 垂旒負扆，竊帝圖王。

translations.literal: Hanging tassels, bearing screen; stole emperor, plotted king.
translations.idiomatic: He took the imperial veil and screen and usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 患生縱敵，難起矜強。

translations.literal: Calamity arose from loosing the foe; hardship rose from priding strength.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster came of sparing a foe; ruin came of boasting his might.

sentences.zh: 丕、登僭假，淪胥以亡。

translations.literal: Pi, Deng usurp-false; sank together thereby to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi and Fu Deng clung to false titles and sank together into oblivion.
